docs.title: Campus API Python
docs.text:
Python SDK for the NYJC Campus school platform: one client for the Campus API (assignments, circles, files, hosted apps, submissions, timetable), Campus Auth (OAuth, login sessions, clients, grants, vaults), Campus Audit (traces, API keys), and the first-party integrations registry.

from campus_python import Campus

campus = Campus()                      # server mode (CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET)

for assignment in campus.api.assignments.list():
    print(assignment.title)

with campus.with_user_session():       # acting as the logged-in user
    campus.api.circles["circle_ab12cd34"].members.add("user_jane", 15)

docs.title: Why it looks like this
docs.text:
• One facade, four service roots. campus.api, campus.auth, campus.audit, and campus.integrations each resolve their own base URL from the environment and carry their own resource tree.
  • Resources are addressable objects. campus.api.circles["circle_ab12cd34"] is a resource you can .get(), .update(), .delete() — and drill into (members, entries, responses, ...). See the Campus API reference.
  • Framework-free. The SDK holds no web-framework dependency and no request state. Flask apps join it through the campus.flask_campus middleware via two injectable seams — see Authentication and Tracing.
  • Errors are typed by status. Every non-2xx response raises an APIError subclass (NotFoundError, ValidationError with field details, ...). See Errors.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The SDK speaks to Campus Auth for every token concern and holds no session state of its own. Pick the lane that matches your host:

Lane Who What you use Server mode backend services CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET Basic auth; with_app_session() for app-identity calls Device flow CLIs, public clients oauth.request_device_code() + wait_for_token() User sessions Flask apps acting as the logged-in user with_user_session() (401 auto-refresh on by default) Token release confidential clients needing upstream tokens broker.token() (token_bridge clients)

docs.title: Server mode
docs.text:
Server-to-server calls authenticate with the OAuth client's Basic credentials (CLIENT_ID / CLIENT_SECRET). You can drive tokens manually — auth.token() for a client_credentials grant, then use_token() — or wrap the work in the app-session context manager, which acquires and releases the token for you:

with campus.with_app_session() as client:
    campus.api.timetable.set_current(timetable_id)
# Authorization is cleared on exit

docs.title: Device flow (public clients)
docs.text:
Public clients (the CLI, desktop tools) have no secret. The RFC 8628 flow walks the user through a verification page:

from campus_python import Campus, errors

campus = Campus(mode="device")

code = campus.auth.oauth.request_device_code(client_id="campus-cli")
print("Enter this code:", code["user_code"], "at", code["verification_uri"])

token = campus.auth.oauth.wait_for_token(
    client_id="campus-cli",
    device_code=code["device_code"],
    interval=code.get("interval"),
    on_pending=lambda: print(".", end=""),   # progress hook per poll
)
campus.use_token(token)

wait_for_token() implements the full polling loop: authorization_pending keeps polling, slow_down raises the interval by 5s for the rest of the flow, network/5xx failures retry until the final attempt, and every other error is fatal. Error responses are normalized to AuthenticationError with the OAuth error code readable via .oauth_error, across all three shapes the auth server emits (dev envelope, production details-stripped envelope, flat RFC 6749).

Refresh-token grants rotate server-side: present a stored token once via auth.refresh(stored) and persist the returned pair before reusing the stale one. Revoke with oauth.revoke() (RFC 7009 — the server answers 200 whether or not the token existed).

docs.title: User sessions
docs.text:
A login session (created by the browser flow in campus.flask_campus via logins.new()) lets server code act as that user. Inside the session context manager every call carries the user's bearer, and an expired bearer is re-acquired once automatically:

with campus.with_user_session() as client:            # 401 auto-refresh ON
    campus.api.submissions["sub_ab12"].unsubmit()

with campus.with_user_session(refresh_on_401=False) as client:  # legacy behaviour
    ...

How the pieces work:

  • The session id resolves explicit argument > installed provider (set_session_id_provider(); flask_campus installs one). With neither, methods raise AuthenticationError naming the seam.
  • auth.get_token() / logins.token() re-acquire the session user's bearer via POST /auth/v1/logins/<session_id>/token — one Basic-authenticated call; an expired grant token is rotated server-side, a missing one raises invalid_grant (re-login required).
  • The 401 hook retries the original request once with the fresh bearer. It cannot double-execute work: Campus authenticates in a before_request hook before any handler runs, so a 401 means no handler executed.

docs.title: Manual bearer control
docs.text:
Any client can be pointed at a token you obtained elsewhere (e.g. a CLI storing tokens in a keyring):

campus.api.client.set_bearer_authorization(access_token)
campus.auth.client.set_bearer_authorization(access_token)
# ...
campus.revoke_session()   # clear Authorization on both

use_token() sets both roots in one call. Raw CampusRequest users (public clients driving auth.refresh) can install their own 401 hook:

client.set_unauthorized_hook(
    lambda: campus.auth.refresh(stored, client_id="campus-cli").access_token
)

docs.title: Upstream tokens (broker)
docs.text:
Confidential clients flagged token_bridge can release the bearer's upstream access tokens (never refresh tokens) for Google and other connected providers:

token = campus.auth.broker.token("google", integration="classroom",
                                 min_scopes=["classroom.rosters.read"])

Denials are typed: 403 carries details.missing_scopes, 401 maps to AuthenticationError. Users inspect and revoke their own grants via connections (connections["google"].delete(user_id=...) — disconnecting the campus provider itself is logout and is rejected server-side).

docs.title: Hosting in a Flask app
docs.text:
The SDK owns transport and tokens; the campus.flask_campus middleware (in the campus repo) owns the browser login flow and client-side session storage. The two layers join through injectable providers:

Concern Owner How the SDK sees it Login flow (authorize / code exchange / logout) campus.flask_campus.context orchestrates this SDK's pure API calls (sessions.new, exchange_code_for_token, logins.new, ...) Session-id storage (browser session keys) campus.flask_campus.context set_session_id_provider() — ids resolve explicit argument > provider Request-context trace headers campus.flask_campus.propagation tracing.set_request_context_provider() — see Tracing User-session token lane this SDK with_user_session() — pure orchestration; the session id arrives via the provider above

Non-Flask hosts need none of this: the CLI authenticates via device flow, stores tokens in its own keyring, and sets bearers directly.

docs.title: Custom clients
docs.text: The SDK talks to Campus through two abstract interfaces in campus_python.json_client. The default implementation is CampusRequest (requests-based, with trace propagation and the optional 401 auto-refresh hook), but any host can bring its own transport — the interfaces were designed to wrap flask.testing.FlaskClient as much as requests.

docs.title: The JsonClient contract
docs.text:
A client must implement:

  • the six verbs — get, post, put, put_data (raw, non-JSON body — file/hosted-app uploads), delete, patch — each returning a JsonResponse;
  • authorization control: the authorization property plus set_basic_authorization(), set_bearer_authorization(), and reset_authorization() (the session managers swap tokens through these);
  • a base_url.

docs.title: campus_python.json_client.interface.JsonClient
docs.text:
Bases: ABC

This class describes the public interface required from Client classes, which are used to send JSON requests.

Optional capability, not part of this abstract interface: concrete clients may support a 401 auto-refresh hook (CampusRequest.set_unauthorized_hook, issue #89) that refreshes the bearer token and retries a request once when it comes back 401. Callers must feature-detect (hasattr) rather than assume it.

Source code in campus_python/json_client/interface.py 
class JsonClient(ABC):
    """This class describes the public interface required from Client
    classes, which are used to send JSON requests.

    Optional capability, not part of this abstract interface: concrete
    clients may support a 401 auto-refresh hook
    (CampusRequest.set_unauthorized_hook, issue #89) that refreshes the
    bearer token and retries a request once when it comes back 401.
    Callers must feature-detect (hasattr) rather than assume it.
    """
    base_url: str
    # pylint: disable=unnecessary-ellipsis

    @abstractmethod
    def __init__(
            self,
            base_url: str | None = None,
            *,
            auth: Iterable[str] | str | None = None,
            headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
            **kwargs: Any
    ): ...

    @abstractmethod
    def reset_authorization(self) -> None:
        """Reset authorization back to client credentials from env."""

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def authorization(self) -> str | None:
        """The current Authorization header value, or None when unset."""

    @abstractmethod
    def set_basic_authorization(self, client_id: str, secret: str) -> None:
        """Set Basic Authorization header using a pre-encoded token.

        Args:
            client_id (str): Client ID.
            secret (str): Client Secret.
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def set_bearer_authorization(self, token: str) -> None:
        """Set Bearer Authorization header.

        Args:
            token (str): Bearer token.
        """

    def set_default_header(self, name: str, value: str) -> None:
        """Set a default header sent with every request (#837).

        Optional capability: the ABC default refuses, so callers can
        detect a client that cannot carry default headers instead of
        silently dropping them. Implementations should set the header
        on their underlying transport (e.g. the requests session).
        """
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} does not support default headers"
        )

    @abstractmethod
    def get(self: Self, path: str, query: JsonDict | None = None) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a GET request."""

    @abstractmethod
    def post(self: Self, path: str, json: JsonDict | None = None) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a POST request."""

    @abstractmethod
    def put(
            self: Self,
            path: str,
            json: JsonDict | None = None,
            query: JsonDict | None = None
    ) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a PUT request."""

    @abstractmethod
    def put_data(
            self: Self,
            path: str,
            data: bytes | str,
            content_type: str | None = None,
            query: JsonDict | None = None
    ) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a PUT request with a raw (non-JSON) body.

        The body is sent verbatim, with no JSON encoding; the
        Content-Type header is caller-controlled. Used by file
        uploads (campus.api /files by-slug), which carry raw bytes
        with an explicit Content-Type. `query` carries URL query
        parameters (e.g. the files upsert's optional display name).
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def post_data(
            self: Self,
            path: str,
            data: bytes | str,
            content_type: str | None = None,
            query: JsonDict | None = None
    ) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a POST request with a raw (non-JSON) body.

        Symmetric with put_data(): the body is sent verbatim, with no
        JSON encoding; the Content-Type header is caller-controlled.
        Used by raw-content create routes that mint server-side ids
        (campus.api timetable attachment uploads), which carry raw
        bytes with an explicit Content-Type. `query` carries URL
        query parameters (e.g. the attachment's original filename).
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def delete(
            self: Self,
            path: str,
            json: JsonDict | None = None,
            query: JsonDict | None = None
    ) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a DELETE request."""

    @abstractmethod
    def patch(
            self: Self,
            path: str,
            json: Any = None,
            query: JsonDict | None = None
    ) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a PATCH request."""

docs.title: The JsonResponse contract
docs.text: Responses expose status_code, headers, text, content (bytes — file content is binary; callers decode), and json(). Implement raise_for_status() by delegating to the base-class mapping: it parses the Campus error envelope (and the legacy error_code form) into the right APIError subclass, recovering OAuth errors from AUTH_* codes when production strips envelope details.

docs.title: campus_python.json_client.interface.JsonResponse
docs.text:
Bases: ABC

This class describes the public interface required from Response wrappers for JSON responses.

Source code in campus_python/json_client/interface.py 
class JsonResponse(ABC):
    """This class describes the public interface required from Response
    wrappers for JSON responses.
    """
    # pylint: disable=unnecessary-ellipsis

    @abstractmethod
    def __init__(self): ...

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def status_code(self) -> int:
        """HTTP status code of the response."""
        ...

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def headers(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Returns headers of the response as a dict."""
        ...

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def text(self) -> str:
        """Returns the response body as a string."""
        ...

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def content(self) -> bytes:
        """Returns the response body as bytes, undecoded.

        File content (campus.api /files) is binary: callers decode,
        never this property.
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def json(self) -> Any:
        """Returns the response body as JSON."""
        ...

    def ok(self) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the response status code is 2xx, False otherwise."""
        return 200 <= self.status_code < 300

    def is_client_error(self) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the response status code is 4xx, False otherwise."""
        return 400 <= self.status_code < 500

    def is_server_error(self) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the response status code is 5xx, False otherwise."""
        return 500 <= self.status_code < 600

    def raise_for_status(self) -> None:
        """Raise the mapped APIError subclass on a 4xx/5xx status.

        Parses the Campus error envelope (and the legacy error_code
        form) into the registered error class for the status code;
        OAuth errors are recovered from AUTH_* codes when the server
        strips envelope details. Response headers and body ride along
        as error notes.
        """
        if not (self.is_client_error() or self.is_server_error()):
            return

        status_code = self.status_code

        # Try to extract a useful message/body
        try:
            response_data = self.json()
        except Exception:
            response_data = None

        try:
            body = response_data if response_data is not None else self.text
        except Exception:
            body = f"HTTP {status_code}"

        error = errors.APIError.with_status_code(status_code, response_data)
        if error:
            # Attach notes for debugging (headers, body)
            # Try the notes attribute first (new APIError)
            try:
                error.notes = {"headers": dict(self.headers), "body": body}
            except AttributeError:
                # Fall back to add_note for older implementations
                try:
                    error.add_note(f"Headers: {self.headers}")
                    error.add_note(f"Body: {body}")
                except Exception:
                    # add_note may not exist; ignore if it doesn't
                    pass
            raise error from None

docs.title: Optional capabilities
docs.text:
Two capabilities are deliberately not part of the ABC. Feature-detect them instead of assuming:

  • Default headers — client.set_default_header(name, value) (#837). The ABC default raises NotImplementedError, so a client that cannot carry default headers refuses loudly rather than dropping them.
  • 401 auto-refresh hook — client.set_unauthorized_hook(fn) (#89). Present on CampusRequest (and used by with_user_session(), which feature-detects via isinstance). The hook runs at most once per request: return the new bearer token to retry with, or None to surface the original 401.

docs.title: The default transport
docs.text: CampusRequest is the requests-based client the facade builds; its optional capabilities (set_default_header, set_unauthorized_hook) are what custom clients may mirror.

docs.title: campus_python.json_client.CampusRequest
docs.text:
Bases: JsonClient

Campus JSON client

This client is pre-configured to handle JSON requests and responses. It provides convenience methods for common HTTP methods with JSON payloads.

Note that the client requires authorization before it can make requests. Use CampusRequest.set_basic_authorization(), CampusRequest.set_bearer_authorization(), or CampusRequest.for_user() to authorize the client, and CampusRequest.reset_authorization() to reset to client credentials

class CampusRequest(JsonClient):
    """Campus JSON client

    This client is pre-configured to handle JSON requests and responses.
    It provides convenience methods for common HTTP methods with JSON
    payloads.

    Note that the client requires authorization before it can make
    requests. Use CampusRequest.set_basic_authorization(),
    CampusRequest.set_bearer_authorization(), or
    CampusRequest.for_user() to authorize the client, and
    CampusRequest.reset_authorization() to reset to client credentials
    """

    def __init__(
            self,
            base_url: str | None,
            *,
            mode: str = "server",
            headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
            **kwargs: Any,
    ):
        self.base_url = base_url or ""
        self._headers = dict(headers or {})
        # allow optional default timeout via kwargs
        self._timeout = kwargs.get("timeout", 10)
        # Optional 401 auto-refresh hook (issue #89); see
        # set_unauthorized_hook(). Off by default.
        self._unauthorized_hook: Callable[[], str | None] | None = None
        self._in_unauthorized_hook = False
        # Session to persist headers and connection pooling
        self._session = requests.Session()
        self._session.headers.update(self._headers)
        # Propagate campus trace context on calls made while the host app
        # handles a traced request, so receiving campus services record
        # them as child spans (campus#816). No-op outside a request
        # context (startup, background threads).
        from .. import tracing

        tracing.instrument_requests_session(self._session)
        # Only set client credentials in server mode
        # Device mode starts without auth (Bearer token will be set later)
        if mode == "server":
            self.reset_authorization()

    @property
    def headers(self) -> HttpHeader:
        """Get the currently configured headers."""
        headers = cast(Mapping[str, str], self._session.headers)
        return HttpHeader.from_header(headers)

    def _build_url(self, path: str) -> str:
        if not self.base_url:  # relative URL
            return f"http://localhost:{env.get('PORT', '8080')}" + path
        if self.base_url.endswith("/") and path.startswith("/"):
            return self.base_url[:-1] + path
        if not self.base_url.endswith("/") and not path.startswith("/"):
            return self.base_url + "/" + path
        return self.base_url + path

    def reset_authorization(self) -> None:
        """Reset authorization back to client credentials from env."""
        env.require("CLIENT_ID", "CLIENT_SECRET")
        self.set_basic_authorization(
            client_id=env.CLIENT_ID,
            secret=env.CLIENT_SECRET
        )

    @property
    def authorization(self) -> str | None:
        """The current Authorization header value, or None when unset."""
        return self._session.headers.get("Authorization")

    def set_basic_authorization(self, client_id: str, secret: str) -> None:
        """Set Basic Authorization header using a pre-encoded token.

        Args:
            client_id (str): Client ID.
            secret (str): Client Secret.
        """
        credentials = f"{client_id}:{secret}"
        # Encode credentials in base64 following RFC 7617
        encoded_credentials = base64.b64encode(
            credentials.encode('utf-8')
        ).decode('ascii')
        self._session.headers["Authorization"] = "Basic " + encoded_credentials

    def set_bearer_authorization(self, token: str) -> None:
        """Set Bearer Authorization header.

        Args:
            token (str): Bearer token.
        """
        self._session.headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + token

    def set_default_header(self, name: str, value: str) -> None:
        """Set a default header sent with every request from this client.

        Non-browser clients use this to present stable identity on API
        calls, e.g. X-Campus-Device (#837) for device attribution of
        spans. Calls made inside a host request context may still add
        per-request headers on top (tracing.propagation_headers).
        """
        self._session.headers[name] = value

    def set_unauthorized_hook(
            self,
            hook: Callable[[], str | None] | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Install a 401 auto-refresh hook (issue #89).

        When a request comes back 401, the hook is invoked once; if it
        returns a bearer token, the Authorization header is refreshed
        and the request is retried once with it. A second 401 on the
        retry is returned to the caller as-is, and a hook returning
        None (refresh failed) leaves the original 401 response in
        place — failures surface exactly as they would without the
        hook.

        The hook runs at most once per request, and never re-enters
        itself: requests made from inside the hook skip the hook, so a
        hook that calls back into this client cannot recurse.

        Args:
            hook: Callable returning the new bearer token, or None to
                signal refresh failure. None clears the hook.
        """
        self._unauthorized_hook = hook

    def _send(self, method: str, url: str, **kwargs: Any) -> JsonResponse:
        """Send a request, with one 401-triggered retry (issue #89).

        The retry is safe even for non-idempotent requests: Campus
        services validate the bearer in a before_request authenticator
        before dispatching, so a 401 response is produced by the auth
        layer before any handler runs — there is no partial work to
        replay.
        """
        try:
            resp = self._session.request(
                method, url, timeout=self._timeout, **kwargs
            )
            if (
                    resp.status_code == 401
                    and self._unauthorized_hook is not None
                    and not self._in_unauthorized_hook
            ):
                self._in_unauthorized_hook = True
                try:
                    token = self._unauthorized_hook()
                finally:
                    self._in_unauthorized_hook = False
                if token:
                    self.set_bearer_authorization(token)
                    resp = self._session.request(
                        method, url, timeout=self._timeout, **kwargs
                    )
        except requests.RequestException as exc:
            raise errors.ServerError(error_description=str(exc)) from None
        return CampusResponse(resp)

    def get(
            self: Self,
            path: str,
            query: JsonDict | None = None
    ) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a GET request."""
        url = self._build_url(path)
        if query:
            return self._send("GET", url, params=query)
        return self._send("GET", url)

    def post(self: Self, path: str, json: JsonDict | None = None) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a POST request."""
        url = self._build_url(path)
        return self._send("POST", url, json=json)

    def put(
            self: Self,
            path: str,
            json: JsonDict | None = None,
            query: JsonDict | None = None
    ) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a PUT request."""
        url = self._build_url(path)
        return self._send("PUT", url, json=json, params=query)

    def put_data(
            self: Self,
            path: str,
            data: bytes | str,
            content_type: str | None = None,
            query: JsonDict | None = None
    ) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a PUT request with a raw body (e.g. file bytes).

        Unlike put(), the body is sent verbatim with no JSON encoding;
        Content-Type is caller-controlled (requests' own default
        applies when omitted).

        Args:
            path: Request path.
            data: Raw request body.
            content_type: Content-Type header for the body, or None to
                leave it to the transport default.
            query: Optional URL query parameters.
        """
        url = self._build_url(path)
        headers = {"Content-Type": content_type} if content_type else None
        return self._send("PUT", url, data=data, headers=headers,
                          params=query)

    def post_data(
            self: Self,
            path: str,
            data: bytes | str,
            content_type: str | None = None,
            query: JsonDict | None = None
    ) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a POST request with a raw body (e.g. file bytes).

        Unlike post(), the body is sent verbatim with no JSON encoding;
        Content-Type is caller-controlled (requests' own default
        applies when omitted).

        Args:
            path: Request path.
            data: Raw request body.
            content_type: Content-Type header for the body, or None to
                leave it to the transport default.
            query: Optional URL query parameters.
        """
        url = self._build_url(path)
        headers = {"Content-Type": content_type} if content_type else None
        return self._send("POST", url, data=data, headers=headers,
                          params=query)

    def delete(
            self: Self,
            path: str,
            json: JsonDict | None = None,
            query: JsonDict | None = None
    ) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a DELETE request."""
        url = self._build_url(path)
        return self._send("DELETE", url, json=json, params=query)

    def patch(
            self: Self,
            path: str,
            json: Any = None,
            query: JsonDict | None = None
    ) -> JsonResponse:
        """Sends a PATCH request."""
        url = self._build_url(path)
        return self._send("PATCH", url, json=json, params=query)

docs.title: Building one
docs.text:
The interfaces exist so hosts can point the SDK at an in-process WSGI app (unit/integration tests without a network) or an exotic transport. The shape:

from campus_python.json_client.interface import JsonClient, JsonResponse

class FlaskTestClientResponse(JsonResponse):
    def __init__(self, response):
        self._response = response          # werkzeug.test.TestResponse
    # implement status_code / headers / text / content / json()
    # and reuse JsonResponse.raise_for_status (do not override)

class FlaskTestClient(JsonClient):
    def __init__(self, test_client, base_url="https://campus.test"):
        self.base_url = base_url
        self._client = test_client
    # implement the six verbs as test_client.open(...) calls,
    # plus the authorization methods

Then construct the service roots directly against it:

from campus_python.api.v1 import ApiRoot

api = ApiRoot(json_client=FlaskTestClient(flask_app.test_client()))
api.assignments.list()

The repo's own test suite stays one level simpler: resource unit tests drive Mock clients through the shared factories in tests/support.py (make_api, make_auth, json_response), pinning recorded calls rather than running a real WSGI stack.

docs.title: Extending the SDK
docs.text: New resources and endpoints follow one pattern: a module in the service's v1/ package defines a ResourceCollection (the URL collection), a nested Resource (a single item), and thin methods that send one request each. This page is the toolkit + conventions; the reference for every base class is embedded below.

docs.title: The three-line method
docs.text:
Endpoint methods send through the Transport verb helpers, keep the envelope key inline, and map records to models at the call site:

class Circles(ResourceCollection):
    path = "circles"

    def list(self) -> "list[campus.model.Circle]":
        body = self._get_json(self.make_path())          # GET; raises on 4xx/5xx
        return [campus.model.Circle.from_resource(item) for item in body["data"]]

    def new(self, *, name: str, tag: str, ...) -> campus.model.Circle:
        return campus.model.Circle.from_resource(self._post_json(
            self.make_path(),
            json=payload(name=name, tag=tag, description=description, parents=parents),
        ))

Helpers available on every resource class:

  • _get_json / _post_json / _put_json / _patch_json / _delete_json — send one verb, raise the mapped APIError on 4xx/5xx, return the parsed body. None query/json kwargs are omitted from the wire call.
  • payload(**fields) — request body dropping None fields (provided falsy values survive).
  • updates(**fields) — same, plus the non-empty guard PATCH routes require. Neither helper can send an explicit null — build bodies like {"submitted_at": null} by hand (see Submissions.unsubmit).
  • When a method must inspect the raw response first (map 404 → KeyError, shape a 400 error, observe rate-limit headers), skip the helpers and call self.client.<verb>() + raise_for_status() directly — see vaults.Vault.__getitem__, oauth.poll_for_token, traces.ingest.

docs.title: Request bodies
docs.text:
json=payload(title=title, description=description, questions=questions)
  • An omitted (None) field is left unchanged upstream — the convention across Campus write routes.
  • Convert only methods where None means omit. Deliberate exceptions in the codebase: unsubmit (explicit null), timetable.new (nested metadata/data body), sessions.new (str() coercion), and required-only literals where the helper adds nothing.
  • Clients.update uses payload() without updates() — the auth server accepts its empty PATCHes; don't add guards the server doesn't have.

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
• Collections end with a trailing slash (make_path default); item routes carry one too; dead-end action/sub-resource parts (submit, add, revoke, entries) do not — mirror the upstream Flask route rules (strict_slashes makes these load-bearing).
  • Collection path attrs carry no slashes (path = "circles").
  • join_path(*parts) strips ends and single-slashes the join; inner slashes survive — by-slug tails rely on that. Don't build paths by raw f-string; go through make_path.
  • Nested sub-resources are addressed by __getitem__ (id) and properties (fixed segment): Circles.Circle.CircleMembers("members", parent=self).

docs.title: Response envelopes
docs.text: Envelope keys (data, value, timetable, entries, users, clients, connections, grant, spans, key, secret, swept_count, ...) are upstream-driven and stay inline at each method — no hidden unwrap layer. A wrong key is a KeyError right in the method that owns it; the unit tests pin every shape.

docs.title: By-slug surfaces
docs.text:
Resources whose records are addressed by a terminal slug path tail (files, hosted apps) subclass BySlugCollection instead, parameterized by record type. The raw-tail rule (slugs ride unquoted — the whole tail after by-slug/ is the slug) and the list/get_meta/get_content/put_by_slug/delete_by_slug surface are defined once:

class HostedApps(BySlugCollection[campus.model.HostedApp]):
    path = "hostedapps"

    def _from_resource(self, record: dict) -> campus.model.HostedApp:
        return campus.model.HostedApp.from_resource(record)

Dict-returning surfaces (Files(BySlugCollection[dict])) need no override at all.

docs.title: Testing it
docs.text:
Unit tests drive a Mock client through the shared factories and pin exact recorded calls:

from tests.support import json_response, make_api

def test_list_unwraps_data_envelope(self):
    api, client = make_api()
    client.get.return_value = json_response({"data": [CIRCLE_RESOURCE]})
    circles = api.circles.list()
    client.get.assert_called_once_with("/api/v1/circles/")
    self.assertEqual(len(circles), 1)

json_response(body, status_code=400) raises the mapped APIError from raise_for_status() — use it for error-path tests.

campus.client.interface

Interface descriptions for the Campus client interface.

This interface is designed to: - wrap flask.testing.FlaskClient - wrap most common client interfaces e.g. requests - provide a common Response interface that wraps werkzeug.test.TestResponse,requests.Response`, etc - so aa to enable WSGI hooks or unit testing with a local WSGI app.

docs.text:
Bases: Transport

Root of all resources.

This class is used to group all top-level resources together.

Source code in campus_python/interface.py 
class ResourceRoot(Transport):
    """Root of all resources.

    This class is used to group all top-level resources together.
    """
    _client: Optional[JsonClient] = None
    url_prefix: str

    def __init__(self, json_client: Optional[JsonClient] = None):
        self._client = json_client

    @property
    def base_url(self) -> str:
        """Get the base URL for this resource root."""
        if not self._client:
            raise AttributeError("No client defined")
        return self._client.base_url

    @property
    def client(self) -> JsonClient:
        """Get the JsonClient associated with this resource root."""
        if not self._client:
            raise AttributeError(
                f"No client defined for {self}"
            )
        return self._client

    def make_path(self, part: str | None = None) -> str:
        """Create a full path for the resource root or a sub-resource.

        Only leading slashes are trimmed here: a url_prefix that
        intentionally ends with a slash (e.g. /integrations/v1/) keeps
        it, and a part with an inner path tail (e.g. broker's
        "google/classroom") is preserved verbatim.

class ResourceCollection(Transport):
    """Collection of resources.

    This class is used to group related resources together.
    """
    _client: Optional[JsonClient] = None
    path: str
    root: ResourceRoot

    def __init__(
            self,
            client: Optional[JsonClient] = None,
            *,
            root: ResourceRoot
    ):
        self._client = client
        self.root = root

    @property
    def client(self) -> JsonClient:
        """Get the JsonClient associated with this resource."""
        if self._client:
            return self._client
        if self.root.client:
            return self.root.client
        raise AttributeError(f"No client defined for {self}")

    def make_path(self, part: str | None = None, end_slash: bool = True) -> str:
        """Create a full path for a resource collection.

        Collection routes carry a trailing slash by default (the
        upstream API schema); item ids, sub-resources and action parts
        append after the collection segment.

        Args:
            part: Optional sub-resource or action path.
            end_slash: Whether to add a trailing slash.

        Returns:
            Full path for the resource collection or sub-resource.
        """
        if part:
            path = join_path(self.root.make_path(self.path), part)
        else:
            path = join_path(self.root.make_path(self.path))
        if end_slash and not path.endswith(SLASH):
            path += SLASH
        return path

    def make_url(self, part: str | None = None) -> str:
        """Create a full URL for the collection or a sub-resource."""
        return f"{self.client.base_url}{self.make_path(part)}"

class Resource(Transport):
    """Resource class that represents API resources

    The resource class uses a JsonClient instance to handle all API requests.
    It only tracks the path of the current resource.
    """
    _client: Optional[JsonClient] = None
    parent: "Resource | ResourceCollection"
    path: str

    def __init__(
            self,
            *parts: str,
            parent: "Resource | ResourceCollection",
            client: Optional[JsonClient] = None,
    ):
        self._client = client
        self.parent = parent
        self.path = parent.make_path(SLASH.join(parts))

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Resource(client={self.client}, path={self.path})"

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.path

    @property
    def client(self) -> JsonClient:
        """Get the JsonClient associated with this resource."""
        if self._client:
            return self._client
        if self.parent and self.parent.client:
            return self.parent.client
        raise AttributeError(f"No client defined for {self}")

    def make_path(self, part: str | None = None, end_slash=False) -> str:
        """Create a full path for a sub-resource or action.

        Item paths built from a parent collection carry the
        collection's trailing slash; dead-end sub-resource and action
        parts append after the item segment without one by default.
        With no part, the instance path is returned as constructed —
        only a leading slash is trimmed, so an item's trailing slash
        survives.
        """
        if part:
            path = join_path(self.path, part)
        else:
            path = SLASH + self.path.lstrip(SLASH)
        if end_slash and not path.endswith(SLASH):
            path += SLASH
        return path

    def make_url(self, part: str | None = None) -> str:
        """Create a full URL for this resource or a sub-resource."""
        return f"{self.client.base_url}{self.make_path(part)}"

def join_path(*parts: str) -> str:
    """Join path parts into a single absolute path.

    Leading/trailing slashes are stripped from each part (inner
    slashes survive — by-slug path tails rely on them), the parts are
    joined with single slashes, and the result gets one leading slash.
    """
    cleaned = [part.strip(SLASH) for part in parts]
    return SLASH + SLASH.join(part for part in cleaned if part)

def payload(**fields: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build a JSON request body from keyword fields.

    Fields set to None are omitted — the "not provided" convention
    across Campus write routes (an omitted field is left unchanged
    upstream). Fields that ARE provided are sent verbatim, including
    falsy ones (0, "", False).

    Not for bodies that must carry an explicit null: build those by
    hand (e.g. submissions.unsubmit's {"submitted_at": null}).
    """
    return {key: value for key, value in fields.items() if value is not None}

def updates(**fields: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build a PATCH body from keyword fields, dropping None fields.

    Raises ValueError when every field is None — Campus PATCH routes
    reject an empty body outright.

    The same explicit-null caveat as payload applies: a PATCH that
    must set a field to null cannot go through here.
    """
    body = payload(**fields)
    if not body:
        raise ValueError("At least one field must be provided for update")
    return body

docs.text:
campus_python.api.v1.byslug

Shared base for by-slug consumer surfaces (files #135, hosted apps #141).

By-slug routes are terminal upstream — the whole path tail after <resource>/by-slug/ is the slug — so slugs ride as raw path tails, never quoted or collapsed. Surfaces differ only in what their records deserialize to, which is the _from_resource hook.

docs.title: BySlugCollection
docs.text:
Bases: ResourceCollection, Generic[R]

Collection whose records are addressed by a terminal by-slug tail.

Subclasses set path and, when records deserialize into a campus.model class, override _from_resource (the default passes the raw record dict through). Parameterize the subclass with the record type (BySlugCollection[dict], BySlugCollection[HostedApp]) so the inherited methods return precise types.

Source code in campus_python/api/v1/byslug.py 
class BySlugCollection(ResourceCollection, Generic[R]):
    """Collection whose records are addressed by a terminal by-slug tail.

    Subclasses set `path` and, when records deserialize into a
    campus.model class, override `_from_resource` (the default passes
    the raw record dict through). Parameterize the subclass with the
    record type (`BySlugCollection[dict]`, `BySlugCollection[HostedApp]`)
    so the inherited methods return precise types.
    """

    def _from_resource(self, record: dict) -> Any:
        """Map a raw record dict to this surface's record type.

        Default: pass the record through unchanged (dict-returning
        surfaces). Model-backed surfaces override this, e.g. with
        ``campus.model.HostedApp.from_resource``.
        """
        return record

    def list(self, prefix: str | None = None) -> "list[R]":
        """List records, optionally under a slug prefix.

        Args:
            prefix: Only include records whose slug starts with this
                prefix.

        Returns:
            The records under the ``{"data": [...]}`` envelope, each
            mapped through _from_resource.
        """
        query = {"prefix": prefix} if prefix else None
        body = self._get_json(self.make_path(), query=query)
        return [self._from_resource(record) for record in body["data"]]

    def get_meta(self, slug: str) -> R:
        """Get a record's metadata by slug (upstream's ?meta=1 query).

        Args:
            slug: The record's stable slug, e.g. "apps/quest-dom".

        Returns:
            The record mapped through _from_resource.
        """
        body = self._get_json(self._by_slug_path(slug), query={"meta": "1"})
        return self._from_resource(body)

    def get_content(self, slug: str) -> bytes:
        """Get a record's bytes by slug — the CURRENT version.

        Responses carry an ETag and a short max-age cache header.
        Content is returned undecoded — callers decode.

        Args:
            slug: The record's stable slug.

        Returns:
            The content, as stored at serve time.
        """
        # Raw bytes, not JSON: this one keeps the raw response.
        resp = self.client.get(self._by_slug_path(slug))
        resp.raise_for_status()
        return resp.content

    def put_by_slug(
            self,
            slug: str,
            data: bytes | str,
            content_type: str | None = None,
            name: str | None = None,
    ) -> R:
        """Create or replace a record's content by slug (upsert).

        Replacing an existing slug keeps its address stable — consumers
        rely on this for in-place updates. Attribution
        (uploaded_by_client_id/user_id) is server-side from the
        bearer; user-session calls attribute to the user
        automatically.

        Args:
            slug: The stable slug to create or replace.
            data: Raw content (the request body).
            content_type: MIME type to store and serve back (e.g.
                "text/html"); defaults to the transport's choice and
                upstream stores application/octet-stream when absent.
            name: Optional display name, stored on the record for new
                records (upstream's PUT ?name= parameter).

        Returns:
            The record mapped through _from_resource (201 shape on
            create, 200 shape on replace; identical dict fields).
        """
        query = {"name": name} if name else None
        # Raw request body, not JSON: this one keeps the raw call.
        resp = self.client.put_data(
            self._by_slug_path(slug), data, content_type=content_type,
            query=query,
        )
        resp.raise_for_status()
        return self._from_resource(resp.json())

    def delete_by_slug(self, slug: str) -> None:
        """Delete a record (its metadata and content) by slug.

        Args:
            slug: The slug to delete.
        """
        self._delete_json(self._by_slug_path(slug))
        return None

    def _by_slug_path(self, slug: str) -> str:
        """Path for a by-slug route.

        The slug is a path tail — slashes are part of the slug and
        upstream's ``<path:slug>`` converter expects them literal — so
        it is concatenated unquoted; make_path only trims a
        leading/trailing slash.
        """
        return self.make_path(f"by-slug/{slug}", end_slash=False)

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.11–3.13 (3.14 tested, unofficial bugfix tier)
  • Poetry (or pip, for consumers)
  • Campus service URLs reachable from your environment

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Consumers pin the release wheel by URL (pip resolves it; the release must exist first — see Releases):

# pyproject.toml
campus-api-python = {url = "https://github.com/nyjc-computing/campus-api-python/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/campus_api_python-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl"}

Then poetry install / poetry lock as usual. The SDK depends only on requests and the campus-common / campus-model wheels — it imports no campus-suite module and holds no web framework.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The environment is the source of truth. Campus ships no baked-in deployment topology: an unconfigured service raises ValueError naming the variables to set.

Variable Required Mode Description CLIENT_ID Yes Server OAuth client ID from Campus auth CLIENT_SECRET Yes Server OAuth client secret from Campus auth CAMPUS_AUTH_URL No All Auth service base URL (highest precedence) CAMPUS_API_URL No All API service base URL (highest precedence) CAMPUS_AUDIT_URL No All Audit service base URL (highest precedence) AUDIT_API_KEY Yes (audit) All Audit API key (audit_v1_...), sent as the audit root's Bearer CAMPUS_CLIENT_TIMEOUT No All Request timeout in seconds (default 60); invalid values are logged and ignored CAMPUS_BASE_URL / BASE_URL No All One origin fronting every service (gateway deployments); consulted last

Per-service precedence: CAMPUS_<SERVICE>_URL → <SERVICE>_URL (bare alias) → CAMPUS_BASE_URL → BASE_URL. For local testing set e.g. CAMPUS_AUTH_URL=http://localhost:5000.

docs.title: First calls
docs.text:
Server modeDevice modeUser sessions (Flask hosts) 
from campus_python import Campus

campus = Campus(timeout=30)   # mode="server" is the default

# Campus API
for assignment in campus.api.assignments.list():
    print(assignment.title)

timetable_id = campus.api.timetable.get_current()

# Campus Auth (requires CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET; Basic-authenticated)
client = campus.auth.clients["client_myapp"]
print(client.get().name)

from campus_python import Campus

campus = Campus(mode="device")   # no credentials required

# Public, read-only registry — works without a token
for integration in campus.integrations.list():
    print(integration.provider, integration.connectable)

Authenticating a device client (no secret) is the device flow — after it returns a token, wait_for_token()'s result is applied with use_token().

with campus.with_user_session() as client:
    # every call inside acts as the logged-in user; an expired
    # bearer auto-refreshes once (401 hook, on by default)
    campus.api.submissions.new(assignment_id=aid, student_id=sid, course_id=cid)

Requires a login session id — normally supplied by the campus.flask_campus middleware. See Authentication.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Every non-2xx response raises an APIError subclass mapped by status code — see the Errors reference.

from campus_python import errors

try:
    campus.api.assignments["assignment_404"].get()
except errors.NotFoundError as err:
    print("no such assignment:", err.error_description)
except errors.ValidationError as err:
    for field_err in err.field_errors:
        print(field_err.field, field_err.code, field_err.message)

Auth-related errors carry the OAuth protocol error where one exists: err.oauth_error (e.g. "invalid_grant") survives even when the server strips envelope details in production.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text: The SDK follows the fleet's strict 0.x scheme: patch releases are additive, minor releases are the breaking line. Every release publishes a wheel attached to its GitHub release; cut one by bumping version in pyproject.toml, then pushing an annotated v* tag — the tag message becomes the release body and CI builds the wheel (with a fresh-venv install smoke) automatically.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text: Every SDK call propagates audit trace context — trace, journey, and device headers — so the Campus Audit waterfall shows which host route (or which process boot) fired each campus call. The machinery lives in campus_python.tracing and is on by default; hosts only touch it to install providers or override journey attribution.

docs.title: In-request calls
docs.text:
When the host application is itself traced — its Flask app wired with campus.audit.middleware.init_app — every request it handles becomes an audit span. SDK calls made while handling that request land as child spans of it: the middleware's propagation module installs a request-context provider via set_request_context_provider(), and its output (span/journey/device headers) is attached verbatim to outbound SDK calls.

The SDK itself is framework-free: with no provider installed, calls are treated as out-of-request and carry only the boot journey below.

docs.title: Boot journeys
docs.text:
Every SDK call is a user request, whether that user is human or agent. Calls made outside any request context — startup, background threads — carry a process journey (one uid-journey-... per process boot) plus a process device tag so boot spans attribute to the deploy that produced them:

  • Device id defaults to RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_ID when present.
  • Inside a request, the caller's own journey always wins; the strict fallback only fills the out-of-request gap.

Overrides:

import campus_python.tracing as tracing

tracing.set_process_journey("uid-journey-migration-run")   # attribute to a named journey
tracing.set_process_device("worker-3")                     # override the device tag
tracing.disable_process_journey()                          # or suppress entirely

CAMPUS_PROCESS_JOURNEY=off (also false/0/no) suppresses the boot journey via the environment — useful for tests and operators. propagation_headers() returns what the next SDK call would send, which is handy for assertions in tests.

docs.title: Instrumenting a custom transport
docs.text: The propagation headers are attached by the default CampusRequest transport. If you bring your own JsonClient (see Custom clients), call instrument_requests_session(session) on the underlying requests.Session to get the same header propagation, or attach propagation_headers() to each request yourself.

docs.title: Related seam: session ids
docs.text: Session-id resolution (login/auth-session lanes) is a separate injectable provider — see Authentication › User sessions and set_session_id_provider().

Boot journeys (#114): every SDK call is a user request, whether that user is human or agent — so calls made outside any request context (startup, background threads) carry a process journey, one uid-journey-… per process boot, plus a process device tag (default: RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_ID) so boot spans attribute to the deploy that produced them. docs.title: set_request_context_provider(provider: RequestContextProvider | None) -> None
docs.text:
Install (or clear) the request-context propagation provider.

When installed, propagation_headers() takes the provider's output verbatim for in-request calls (the provider owns the header contract, including device gap-fill) and applies the process boot journey only when the provider reports no active request context (returns None). Pass None to revert to the built-in flask reader.

Source code in campus_python/tracing.py 
def set_request_context_provider(
        provider: RequestContextProvider | None,
) -> None:
    """Install (or clear) the request-context propagation provider.

    When installed, propagation_headers() takes the provider's output
    verbatim for in-request calls (the provider owns the header
    contract, including device gap-fill) and applies the process boot
    journey only when the provider reports no active request context
    (returns None). Pass None to revert to the built-in flask reader.
    """
    global _request_context_provider
    _request_context_provider = provider

def set_process_journey(
        journey_id: str | None = None,
        *,
        name: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Set this process's boot journey explicitly (#114).

    Overrides CAMPUS_PROCESS_JOURNEY and re-enables journeys after
    disable_process_journey(). Mints a uid-journey-… when journey_id is
    omitted (keeping any previously minted/explicit id on later calls);
    a name labels the journey's cards (forwarded as X-Journey-Name,
    campus#952).

    Returns:
        The process journey id now in effect.
    """
    with _process_lock:
        if not _process_state["initialized"]:
            _init_process_state()
        _process_state["disabled"] = False
        if _process_state["journey_id"] is None:
            _process_state["journey_id"] = journey_id or _mint_journey_id()
        elif journey_id is not None:
            _process_state["journey_id"] = journey_id
        if name is not None:
            _process_state["journey_name"] = name
        return _process_state["journey_id"]

def disable_process_journey() -> None:
    """Suppress the boot journey on out-of-request calls (#114).

    For tests and operators who don't want the correlation; the process
    device tag is unaffected. set_process_journey() re-enables.
    """

        if not _process_state["initialized"]:
            _init_process_state()
        _process_state["disabled"] = True

docs.title: propagation_headers() -> dict[str, str]
docs.text:
Headers to attach to an outbound SDK call from the active context.

Empty outside a request context until #114 — now: out-of-request calls carry the process boot journey (X-Journey-ID/X-Journey-Name) and the process device (X-Campus-Device, default RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_ID), so startup and background calls correlate under one journey per boot. Inside a request, the caller's own journey always wins — a journey-less request stays unjourneyed (strict MVP: the trace waterfall already correlates the chain) — and the process device only fills the gap when the request stashed none. The receiving campus service's tracing middleware turns the trace headers into a child span of the caller's span (#794, campus#816); the journeys middleware adopts X-Journey-ID so the child span joins the caller's action journey (campus#828), with X-Journey-Name carrying its human label (campus#952); the tracing middleware adopts X-Campus-Device for the child span's device tag when it knows nothing better (campus#837).

The in-request half resolves from the installed request-context provider (set_request_context_provider); with no provider there is no request-context half — every call is treated as out-of-request and carries only the boot journey (the former built-in flask reader was removed in 0.5.0; flask_campus installs the provider).

Source code in campus_python/tracing.py 
def propagation_headers() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Headers to attach to an outbound SDK call from the active context.

    Empty outside a request context until #114 — now: out-of-request
    calls carry the process boot journey (X-Journey-ID/X-Journey-Name)
    and the process device (X-Campus-Device, default RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_ID),
    so startup and background calls correlate under one journey per boot.
    Inside a request, the caller's own journey always wins — a journey-less
    request stays unjourneyed (strict MVP: the trace waterfall already
    correlates the chain) — and the process device only fills the gap
    when the request stashed none. The receiving campus service's
    tracing middleware turns the trace headers into a child span of the
    caller's span (#794, campus#816); the journeys middleware adopts
    X-Journey-ID so the child span joins the caller's action journey
    (campus#828), with X-Journey-Name carrying its human label
    (campus#952); the tracing middleware adopts X-Campus-Device for the
    child span's device tag when it knows nothing better (campus#837).

    The in-request half resolves from the installed request-context
    provider (set_request_context_provider); with no provider there is
    no request-context half — every call is treated as out-of-request
    and carries only the boot journey (the former built-in flask
    reader was removed in 0.5.0; flask_campus installs the provider).
    """
    headers: dict[str, str] = {}
    request_headers = (
        _request_context_provider() if _request_context_provider else None
    )

    if request_headers is None:
        # Out of any request context (startup, background threads): the
        # boot journey and process device are the only correlation there is.
        journey_id, journey_name, device_id = _process_snapshot()
        if journey_id:
            headers[JOURNEY_ID_HEADER] = journey_id
        if journey_name:
            headers[JOURNEY_NAME_HEADER] = journey_name
        if device_id:
            headers[DEVICE_ID_HEADER] = device_id
        return headers

    headers.update(request_headers)
    return headers

docs.title: instrument_requests_session(session: requests.Session) -> bool
docs.text:
Wrap a requests.Session so its calls carry campus trace context.

Headers are computed at call time from the host's active request context, so a shared session stays correct under concurrent requests. Calls outside a request context (startup, background threads) carry the process boot journey and device (#114); calls inside a request never inherit it (the caller's journey, or none, wins).

Idempotent: re-instrumenting a session is a no-op.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default session Session

The requests.Session to instrument.

required

Returns:

Type Description bool

True if the session was instrumented now, False if already done.

def instrument_requests_session(session: requests.Session) -> bool:
    """Wrap a requests.Session so its calls carry campus trace context.

    Headers are computed at call time from the host's active request
    context, so a shared session stays correct under concurrent requests.
    Calls outside a request context (startup, background threads) carry
    the process boot journey and device (#114); calls inside a request
    never inherit it (the caller's journey, or none, wins).

    Idempotent: re-instrumenting a session is a no-op.

    Args:
        session: The requests.Session to instrument.

    Returns:
        True if the session was instrumented now, False if already done.
    """
    if getattr(session, _INSTRUMENTED_ATTR, False):
        return False

    original_request = session.request

    def request(method, url, **kwargs):
        extra = propagation_headers()
        if extra:
            headers = dict(kwargs.get("headers") or {})
            for name, value in extra.items():
                headers.setdefault(name, value)
            kwargs["headers"] = headers
        return original_request(method, url, **kwargs)

    # Instance-level override of the bound method: every requests verb
    # funnels through Session.request, so one wrap covers all calls.
    typing.cast(typing.Any, session).request = request
    setattr(session, _INSTRUMENTED_ATTR, True)
    return True

docs.title: Campus API (campus.api)
docs.text:
The /api/v1 service: assignments, circles, files, hosted apps, submissions, and timetable. Address collections directly (campus.api.assignments.list()), single items by id (campus.api.circles["circle_ab12cd34"].get()), and drill into sub-resources (... submissions["sub_1"].feedback.add(...)).

All methods raise the mapped APIError subclass on non-2xx responses. Records deserialize to campus.model classes, except files, which are plain validated dicts.

Note: campus.model.* types are documented in the campus repo; signatures here reference them without cross-links.

class Assignments(ResourceCollection):
    """Campus API Assignments resource."""
    path = "assignments"

    def __getitem__(self, assignment_id: str) -> "Assignments.Assignment":
        """Get a specific assignment resource by ID."""
        return Assignments.Assignment(assignment_id, parent=self)

    def list(self, *, created_by: "str | None" = None) -> "list[campus.model.Assignment]":
        """List all assignments matching filter requirements.

        Args:
            created_by: Filter by teacher who created the assignment

        Returns:
            List of Assignment objects
        """
        params = {}
        if created_by:
            params["created_by"] = created_by

        body = self._get_json(self.make_path(), query=params)
        return [
            campus.model.Assignment.from_resource(item)
            for item in body["data"]
        ]

    def new(
            self,
            *,
            title: str,
            description: "str | None" = None,
            questions: "list[dict] | None" = None,
            classroom_links: "list[dict] | None" = None,
    ) -> campus.model.Assignment:
        """Create a new assignment.

        Args:
            title: Assignment title (required by the server).
            description: Assignment description.
            questions: Question definitions.
            classroom_links: Google Classroom course/coursework links.

        Returns:
            The created Assignment.
        """
        return campus.model.Assignment.from_resource(self._post_json(
            self.make_path(),
            json=payload(
                title=title,
                description=description,
                questions=questions,
                classroom_links=classroom_links,
            )
        ))

    class Assignment(Resource):
        """Single campus API assignment resource."""

        @property
        def links(self) -> "Assignments.Assignment.Links":
            """Get the links resource for this assignment."""
            return Assignments.Assignment.Links("links", parent=self)

        def delete(self) -> None:
            """Delete this assignment."""
            self._delete_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))

        def get(self) -> campus.model.Assignment:
            """Get this assignment.

            Returns:
                The Assignment.
            """
            body = self._get_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))
            return campus.model.Assignment.from_resource(body)

        def update(self, **fields) -> None:
            """Update this assignment with the given fields.

            The server rejects an empty PATCH body, so at least one
            field must be provided.
            """
            self._patch_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True), json=updates(**fields))
            return None

        class Links(Resource):
            """Campus API Assignment Links resource."""

            def add(
                    self,
                    *,
                    course_id: str,
                    coursework_id: str,
                    attachment_id: str | None = None,
            ) -> None:
                """Attach a Google Classroom course/coursework link.

                Args:
                    course_id: Classroom course ID.
                    coursework_id: Classroom coursework ID.
                    attachment_id: Optional Drive attachment ID.
                """
                self._post_json(self.make_path(), json=payload(
                    course_id=course_id,
                    coursework_id=coursework_id,
                    attachment_id=attachment_id,
                ))
                return None

            resp = self.client.put_data(

            resp.raise_for_status()

class Submissions(ResourceCollection):
    """Campus API Submissions resource."""
    path = "submissions"

    def __getitem__(self, submission_id: str) -> "Submissions.Submission":
        """Get a specific submission resource by ID."""
        return Submissions.Submission(submission_id, parent=self)

    def list(
            self,
            *,
            assignment_id: "str | None" = None,
            student_id: "str | None" = None,
            course_id: "str | None" = None,
    ) -> "list[campus.model.Submission]":
        """List all submissions matching filter requirements.

        Args:
            assignment_id: Filter by assignment
            student_id: Filter by student
            course_id: Filter by Google Classroom course

        Returns:
            List of Submission objects
        """
        query = {}
        if assignment_id:
            query["assignment_id"] = assignment_id
        if student_id:
            query["student_id"] = student_id
        if course_id:
            query["course_id"] = course_id

        body = self._get_json(self.make_path(), query=query)
        return [
            campus.model.Submission.from_resource(item)
            for item in body["data"]
        ]

    def by_assignment(self, assignment_id: str) -> "list[campus.model.Submission]":
        """List submissions for a specific assignment.

        Args:
            assignment_id: Assignment ID

        Returns:
            List of Submission objects
        """
        path = self.make_path(f"by-assignment/{assignment_id}")
        body = self._get_json(path)
        return [
            campus.model.Submission.from_resource(item)
            for item in body["data"]
        ]

    def by_student(self, student_id: str) -> "list[campus.model.Submission]":
        """List submissions from a specific student.

        Args:
            student_id: Student user ID

        Returns:
            List of Submission objects
        """
        path = self.make_path(f"by-student/{student_id}")
        body = self._get_json(path)
        return [
            campus.model.Submission.from_resource(item)
            for item in body["data"]
        ]

    def new(
            self,
            *,
            assignment_id: str,
            student_id: str,
            course_id: str,
            responses: "list[dict] | None" = None,
    ) -> campus.model.Submission:
        """Create a new submission.

        Args:
            assignment_id: Assignment ID
            student_id: Student user ID
            course_id: Google Classroom course ID
            responses: List of response dictionaries

        Returns:
            Created Submission object
        """
        return campus.model.Submission.from_resource(self._post_json(
            self.make_path(),
            json=payload(
                assignment_id=assignment_id,
                student_id=student_id,
                course_id=course_id,
                responses=responses,
            )
        ))

    class Submission(Resource):
        """Single campus API submission resource."""

        @property
        def responses(self) -> "Submissions.Submission.Responses":
            """Get the responses resource for this submission."""
            return Submissions.Submission.Responses("responses", parent=self)

        @property
        def feedback(self) -> "Submissions.Submission.Feedback":
            """Get the feedback resource for this submission."""
            return Submissions.Submission.Feedback("feedback", parent=self)

        def delete(self) -> None:
            """Delete this submission."""
            self._delete_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))

        def get(self) -> campus.model.Submission:
            """Get this submission."""
            body = self._get_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))
            return campus.model.Submission.from_resource(body)

        def update(
                self,
                *,
                responses: "list[dict] | None" = None,
                feedback: "list[dict] | None" = None,
                submitted_at: "str | None" = None,
        ) -> None:
            """Update this submission.

            All parameters are optional. Only provided fields will be updated.

            Args:
                responses: New list of responses
                feedback: New list of feedback
                submitted_at: New submitted_at timestamp
            """
            self._patch_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True), json=updates(
                responses=responses,
                feedback=feedback,
                submitted_at=submitted_at,
            ))
            return None

        def submit(self) -> None:
            """Finalize/submit this submission (marks submitted_at timestamp)."""
            path = self.make_path("submit", end_slash=False)
            self._post_json(path)
            return None

        def unsubmit(self) -> None:
            """Clear this submission's submitted_at timestamp.

            The server only clears submitted_at for an explicit null in
            the PATCH body; update() cannot express that because None
            means "omit the field" there.
            """
            self._patch_json(
                self.make_path(end_slash=True), json={"submitted_at": None}
            )
            return None

        class Responses(Resource):
            """Campus API Submission Responses resource."""

            def add(
                    self,
                    *,
                    question_id: str,
                    response_text: str,
            ) -> None:
                """Add or update a response to a question.

                Args:
                    question_id: Question ID
                    response_text: Student's response text
                """
                payload = {
                    "question_id": question_id,
                    "response_text": response_text,
                }
                self._post_json(self.make_path(), json=payload)
                return None

        class Feedback(Resource):
            """Campus API Submission Feedback resource."""

            def add(
                    self,
                    *,
                    question_id: str,
                    feedback_text: str,
            ) -> None:
                """Add feedback on a response to a question.

                Args:
                    question_id: Question ID
                    feedback_text: Teacher's feedback text
                """
                payload = {
                    "question_id": question_id,
                    "feedback_text": feedback_text,
                }
                self._post_json(self.make_path(), json=payload)
