class Timetables(ResourceCollection):
    """Campus API Timetable resource."""

    path = "timetable"
    # hardcoded enums
    timeslots = TIMESLOTS
    weekdays = WEEKDAYS

    def __getitem__(self, timetable_id: str) -> "Timetables.Timetable":
        """Get a specific timetable resource by ID."""
        return Timetables.Timetable(timetable_id, parent=self)

    def view(self) -> dict:
        """Get the deployment's timetable pointer state.

        Returns:
            {"current": timetable_id | None, "next": timetable_id |
            None, "effective_from": datetime | None} — the pending
            switch applies at its effective_from without any client
            action (#1075).
        """
        return self._get_json(self.make_path())

    def patch(
        self,
        *,
        current: str | None = None,
        next: str | None = None,  # noqa: A002 - API field name
        effective_from: str | None = None,
    ) -> dict:
        """Patch exactly one timetable pointer (#1075).

        Pass keyword arguments, exactly one of `current` or `next`.

        Args:
            current: Timetable ID to make current, effective now.
            next: Timetable ID to schedule as the pending switch
                (reschedules any previous pending switch).
            effective_from: When the pending switch applies (ISO
                datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for 07:00 school time). Only
                valid with `next`; absent stages an undated switch
                that flips only when pointed at manually.

        Returns:
            The resulting pointer state (same shape as view()).
        """
        present = {
            key: value
            for key, value in (("current", current), ("next", next))
            if value is not None
        }
        if len(present) != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                "Patch exactly one pointer: pass current=<id> or "
                "next=<id> (use cancel_next() to cancel a pending "
                "switch)"
            )
        body: dict = dict(present)
        if "next" in body and effective_from is not None:
            body["effective_from"] = effective_from
        return self._patch_json(self.make_path(), json=body)

    def cancel_next(self) -> dict:
        """Cancel the pending scheduled switch (API: {next: null}).

        Returns:
            The resulting pointer state.
        """
        return self._patch_json(self.make_path(), json={"next": None})

    def me(self, at: str | None = None) -> dict:
        """Resolve the signed-in user's effective timetable view (#592).

        Returns:
            {"current": {timetable_id, lessongroup_id, source},
            "next": null | {..., effective_from, change_type}}; entries
            render via timetable[id].entries filtered by
            lessongroup_id.
        """
        query = {"at": at} if at else None
        return self._get_json(
            self.make_path("me", end_slash=False), query=query
        )

    def new(self, metadata: dict, data: dict) -> dict:
        """Create a new timetable.

        Args:
            metadata: Metadata for the timetable (e.g., start_date, end_date)
            data: Timetable data; must contain the key `lessongroups`
                (not `lesson_groups` — the server rejects the request
                with 400 otherwise)

        Returns:
            The created timetable resource
        """
        if "lessongroups" not in data:
            raise ValueError(
                "data must contain the key 'lessongroups'"
                + (
                    " ('lesson_groups' found instead — rename it)"
                    if "lesson_groups" in data else ""
                )
            )
        body = self._post_json(
            self.make_path(),
            json={
                "metadata": metadata,
                "data": data
            }
        )
        # POST /timetable/ wraps the created resource in a data envelope
        return body["data"]

    def list_metadata(
        self, **filters: typing.Any
    ) -> "list[campus.model.TimetableMetadata]":
        """List timetable metadata records.

        Args:
            **filters: Arbitrary filter parameters applied to the query.

        Returns:
            list[campus.model.TimetableMetadata]: Matching
            timetable metadata objects. (GET /timetable/ itself now
            serves the pointer state; the list lives at
            /timetable/metadata/.)
        """
        body = self._get_json(
            self.make_path("metadata"), query=filters if filters else None
        )
        return [
            campus.model.TimetableMetadata.from_resource(item) for item in body["data"]
        ]

    class Timetable(Resource):
        """A single timetable with start date."""

        @property
        def entries(self) -> "Timetables.Timetable.Entries":
            """Get the entries resource for this timetable."""
            return Timetables.Timetable.Entries("entries", parent=self)

        @property
        def metadata(self) -> "Timetables.Timetable.Metadata":
            """Get the metadata resource for this timetable."""
            return Timetables.Timetable.Metadata("metadata", parent=self)

        @property
        def attachments(self) -> "Timetables.Timetable.Attachments":
            """Get the attachments resource for this timetable."""
            return Timetables.Timetable.Attachments("attachments", parent=self)

        def delete(self) -> None:
            """Delete this timetable version and all of its rows (#1088).

            DELETE /timetable/<id>/ cascades the version's entries, group
            members and lessongroup rows, then the version row itself.
            The API refuses the version the current or next pointer
            names with a 409 — move/cancel the pointer first. This is
            the cleanup surface for the label-drift create 409.
            """
            self._delete_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))
            return None

        def get(self) -> campus.model.Timetable:
            """Get this timetable (metadata and labeled entries).

            GET /timetable/<id>/ wraps the resource in a
            ``{"timetable": ...}`` envelope.
            """
            body = self._get_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))
            return campus.model.Timetable.from_resource(body["timetable"])

        class Entries(Resource):
            """Entries for a single timetable."""

            def list(self) -> "list[campus.model.TimetableEntry]":
                """Return a list of all entries for this timetable."""
                body = self._get_json(self.make_path())
                return [
                    campus.model.TimetableEntry.from_resource(item)
                    for item in body["entries"]
                ]

        class Metadata(Resource):
            """Metadata for a single timetable."""

            def get(self) -> campus.model.TimetableMetadata:
                """Get the metadata for this timetable.

                This does not include timetable entries.
                """
                body = self._get_json(self.make_path())
                return campus.model.TimetableMetadata.from_resource(body)

            def update(
                self,
                *,
                label: str | None = None,
                start_date: str | None = None,
                end_date: str | None = None,
            ) -> campus.model.TimetableMetadata:
                """Update metadata fields for this timetable (subset).

                Only the fields explicitly passed change; call with at
                least one. `label` is the committee's display name —
                to unset it use clear_label() (the API distinguishes
                an absent field from a null one, so this method cannot
                express clearing).

                Args:
                    label: The new display name (omit to leave alone).
                    start_date: New start date (omit to leave alone).
                    end_date: New end date (omit to leave alone).

                Returns:
                    The updated metadata resource.
                """
                body: dict = {}
                if label is not None:
                    body["label"] = label
                if start_date is not None:
                    body["start_date"] = start_date
                if end_date is not None:
                    body["end_date"] = end_date
                if not body:
                    raise ValueError(
                        "Update at least one field: pass label=, "
                        "start_date= or end_date= (use clear_label() "
                        "to unset the label)"
                    )
                response = self._patch_json(self.make_path(), json=body)
                return campus.model.TimetableMetadata.from_resource(response)

            def clear_label(self) -> campus.model.TimetableMetadata:
                """Clear the timetable's display label (label = null).

                Returns:
                    The updated metadata resource.
                """
                response = self._patch_json(self.make_path(), json={"label": None})
                return campus.model.TimetableMetadata.from_resource(response)

        class Attachments(Resource):
            """Attachments for a single timetable (files-backed).

            Each attachment is a files-backend record under the
            version's attachments namespace; the committee's original
            filename rides as the record's display name. Records are
            plain dicts (the files surface's shape), not campus.model
            classes.
            """

            def list(self) -> list[dict]:
                """List this timetable's attachments, newest first.

                Returns:
                    Attachment records (files-backend records); the
                    attachment id is each record's "id".
                """
                body = self._get_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))
                return list(body["data"])

            def upload(
                self,
                data: bytes,
                filename: str,
                content_type: str | None = None,
            ) -> dict:
                """Attach a file (raw bytes) to this timetable.

                Each upload mints a new attachment — re-uploading the
                same filename adds a second copy (removal is explicit).

                Args:
                    data: Raw file content (the request body).
                    filename: The attachment's display filename (the
                        committee's original filename).
                    content_type: MIME type to store and serve back
                        (e.g. "application/pdf"); the transport
                        default applies when omitted.

                Returns:
                    The created attachment record.
                """
                query = {"filename": filename}
                resp = self.client.post_data(
                    self.make_path(end_slash=True),
                    data,
                    content_type=content_type,
                    query=query,
                )
                resp.raise_for_status()
                return resp.json()

            def get_content(self, attachment_id: str) -> bytes:
                """Get an attachment's bytes — the stored version.

                Args:
                    attachment_id: The attachment id (the record's
                        "id").

                Returns:
                    The content, as stored.
                """
                resp = self.client.get(
                    self.make_path(f"{attachment_id}/content", end_slash=True)
                )
                resp.raise_for_status()
                return resp.content

            def delete(self, attachment_id: str) -> None:
                """Remove an attachment (its record and content).

                Args:
                    attachment_id: The attachment id to remove.
                """
                self._delete_json(self.make_path(attachment_id, end_slash=True))
                return None

    def update(
        self,
        *,
        label: str | None = None,
        start_date: str | None = None,
        end_date: str | None = None,
    ) -> campus.model.TimetableMetadata:
        """Update metadata fields for this timetable (subset).

        Only the fields explicitly passed change; call with at
        least one. `label` is the committee's display name —
        to unset it use clear_label() (the API distinguishes
        an absent field from a null one, so this method cannot
        express clearing).

        Args:
            label: The new display name (omit to leave alone).
            start_date: New start date (omit to leave alone).
            end_date: New end date (omit to leave alone).

        Returns:
            The updated metadata resource.
        """
        body: dict = {}
        if label is not None:
            body["label"] = label
        if start_date is not None:
            body["start_date"] = start_date
        if end_date is not None:
            body["end_date"] = end_date
        if not body:
            raise ValueError(
                "Update at least one field: pass label=, "
                "start_date= or end_date= (use clear_label() "
                "to unset the label)"
            )
        response = self._patch_json(self.make_path(), json=body)
        return campus.model.TimetableMetadata.from_resource(response)

        """Clear the timetable's display label (label = null).

        Returns:
            The updated metadata resource.

        return campus.model.TimetableMetadata.from_resource(response)

def patch(
    self,
    *,
    current: str | None = None,
    next: str | None = None,  # noqa: A002 - API field name
    effective_from: str | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Patch exactly one timetable pointer (#1075).

    Pass keyword arguments, exactly one of `current` or `next`.

    Args:
        current: Timetable ID to make current, effective now.
        next: Timetable ID to schedule as the pending switch
            (reschedules any previous pending switch).
        effective_from: When the pending switch applies (ISO
            datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD for 07:00 school time). Only
            valid with `next`; absent stages an undated switch
            that flips only when pointed at manually.

    Returns:
        The resulting pointer state (same shape as view()).
    """
    present = {
        key: value
        for key, value in (("current", current), ("next", next))
        if value is not None
    }
    if len(present) != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            "Patch exactly one pointer: pass current=<id> or "
            "next=<id> (use cancel_next() to cancel a pending "
            "switch)"
        )
    body: dict = dict(present)
    if "next" in body and effective_from is not None:
        body["effective_from"] = effective_from
    return self._patch_json(self.make_path(), json=body)

    """Create a new timetable.

    Args:
        metadata: Metadata for the timetable (e.g., start_date, end_date)

docs.title: Audit (campus.audit)
docs.text:
The /audit/v1 service: trace ingestion and queries, plus management of the audit service's own API keys. The audit root authenticates with an audit_v1_... key (AUDIT_API_KEY) as its Bearer — client-secret Basic auth is rejected by the service.

Ingestion feeds the client-side circuit breaker before raising: a 429 trips the bucket (Retry-After honored), 2xx clears expired trips, and a breaker failure never breaks ingestion. See Tracing for how spans attribute to journeys.

            adds {"failed": [...]} with per-span statuses.

        # breaker failure must never break ingestion.

class APIKeys(ResourceCollection):
    """Campus Audit API keys resource.

    Every write takes a privilege set: either a scope list or a named
    role the service resolves to one.
    """
    path = "apikeys"

    def __getitem__(self, api_key_id: str) -> "APIKeys.APIKey":
        """Get a specific API key resource by ID."""
        return APIKeys.APIKey(api_key_id, parent=self)

    def new(
            self,
            *,
            name: str,
            owner_id: str,
            scopes: "list[str] | None" = None,
            role: "str | None" = None,
            rate_limit: "int | None" = None,
            expires_at: "str | None" = None,
    ) -> JsonDict:
        """Create an API key.

        Give either `scopes` or a named `role` — the service resolves a
        role to exactly one scope list. The two are mutually exclusive
        server-side: sending both is refused (422) rather than one
        silently winning, so this method does not pre-judge them. An
        unknown role is likewise refused, with the server naming the
        roles that exist — the catalogue is the service's, so it is not
        duplicated here.

        Args:
            name: Key name
            owner_id: Owner user ID
            scopes: Scope strings the key grants (e.g. ["traces:read"])
            role: A named role the service resolves to a scope list
            rate_limit: Requests per minute (optional)
            expires_at: ISO 8601 expiry (optional)

        Returns:
            The created key record; its plaintext `api_key` value is
            shown only here.
        """
        return self._post_json(self.make_path(), json=payload(
            name=name,
            owner_id=owner_id,
            scopes=scopes,
            role=role,
            rate_limit=rate_limit,
            expires_at=expires_at,
        ))

    def list(
            self,
            *,
            owner_id: "str | None" = None,
            active_only: bool = True,
            limit: "int | None" = None,
    ) -> JsonDict:
        """List API keys with optional filtering.

        Args:
            owner_id: Filter by owner user ID
            active_only: Only non-expired, non-revoked keys (default True)
            limit: Page size (server default 50)

        Returns:
            {"api_keys": [...], "count": int}
        """
        query: JsonDict = {}
        if owner_id is not None:
            query["owner_id"] = owner_id
        # The server parses bool query values from the lowercase
        # literals true/false (flask_campus _BOOL_LITERALS); Python's
        # str(True) capitalization would 422.
        query["active_only"] = str(active_only).lower()
        if limit is not None:
            query["limit"] = limit
        return self._get_json(self.make_path(), query=query)

    class APIKey(Resource):
        """Single campus audit API key resource.

        update() takes a privilege set too: a scope list or a named
        role.
        """

        def get(self) -> JsonDict:
            """Get this API key's record (no key hash or plaintext)."""
            return self._get_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))

        def update(
                self,
                *,
                name: "str | None" = None,
                scopes: "list[str] | None" = None,
                role: "str | None" = None,
                rate_limit: "int | None" = None,
        ) -> JsonDict:
            """Update this API key's mutable fields.

            Only name, scopes, and rate_limit are mutable; use
            revoke() to disable the key. The server rejects an empty
            update, so at least one field must be provided.

            A `role` re-scopes the key to the scope list the service
            resolves that role to. It is mutually exclusive with
            `scopes` server-side: sending both is refused (422) rather
            than one silently winning, so this method does not
            pre-judge them.

            Returns:
                The updated key record
            """
            return self._patch_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True), json=updates(
                name=name,
                scopes=scopes,
                role=role,
                rate_limit=rate_limit,
            ))

        def revoke(self) -> None:
            """Revoke this API key (the record is kept for audit)."""
            self._delete_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))
            return None

        def regenerate(self) -> str:
            """Regenerate this API key's value.

            The old value stops working immediately.

            Returns:
                The new plaintext key value, shown only here.
            """
            return self._post_json(
                self.make_path("regenerate", end_slash=False)
            )["key"]

        rate_limit: "int | None" = None,
        expires_at: "str | None" = None,
) -> JsonDict:
    """Create an API key.

    Give either `scopes` or a named `role` — the service resolves a
    role to exactly one scope list. The two are mutually exclusive
    server-side: sending both is refused (422) rather than one
    silently winning, so this method does not pre-judge them. An
    unknown role is likewise refused, with the server naming the
    roles that exist — the catalogue is the service's, so it is not
    duplicated here.

    Args:
        name: Key name
        owner_id: Owner user ID
        scopes: Scope strings the key grants (e.g. ["traces:read"])
        role: A named role the service resolves to a scope list
        rate_limit: Requests per minute (optional)
        expires_at: ISO 8601 expiry (optional)

    Returns:
        The created key record; its plaintext `api_key` value is
        shown only here.
    """
    return self._post_json(self.make_path(), json=payload(
        name=name,
        owner_id=owner_id,
        scopes=scopes,
        role=role,
        rate_limit=rate_limit,
        expires_at=expires_at,
    ))

def list(
        self,
        *,
        owner_id: "str | None" = None,
        active_only: bool = True,
        limit: "int | None" = None,
) -> JsonDict:
    """List API keys with optional filtering.

    Args:
        owner_id: Filter by owner user ID
        active_only: Only non-expired, non-revoked keys (default True)
        limit: Page size (server default 50)

    Returns:
        {"api_keys": [...], "count": int}
    """
    query: JsonDict = {}
    if owner_id is not None:
        query["owner_id"] = owner_id
    # The server parses bool query values from the lowercase
    # literals true/false (flask_campus _BOOL_LITERALS); Python's
    # str(True) capitalization would 422.
    query["active_only"] = str(active_only).lower()
    if limit is not None:
        query["limit"] = limit
    return self._get_json(self.make_path(), query=query)

class AuthRoot(ResourceRoot):
    """Campus Auth resource."""
    url_prefix: str = "/auth/v1"

    def __init__(self, json_client: JsonClient):
        super().__init__(json_client=json_client)
        self._broker = None
        self._clients = None
        self._connections = None
        self._credentials = None
        self._grants = None
        self._logins = None
        self._oauth = None
        self._root = None
        self._sessions = None
        self._users = None
        self._vaults = None

    @property
    def broker(self) -> broker.Broker:
        """Get the token broker resource."""
        if not self._broker:
            self._broker = broker.Broker(root=self)
        return self._broker

    @property
    def clients(self) -> clients.Clients:
        """Get the clients resource."""
        if not self._clients:
            self._clients = clients.Clients(root=self)
        return self._clients

    @property
    def connections(self) -> connections.Connections:
        """Get the connections resource."""
        if not self._connections:
            self._connections = connections.Connections(root=self)
        return self._connections

    @property
    def credentials(self) -> credentials.Credentials:
        """Get the credentials resource."""
        if not self._credentials:
            self._credentials = credentials.Credentials(root=self)
        return self._credentials

    @property
    def logins(self) -> logins.LoginSessions:
        """Get the logins resource."""
        if not self._logins:
            self._logins = logins.LoginSessions(root=self)
        return self._logins

    @property
    def oauth(self) -> oauth.OAuth:
        """Get the OAuth resource for device authorization flow."""
        if not self._oauth:
            self._oauth = oauth.OAuth(root=self)
        return self._oauth

    @property
    def root(self) -> root.Root:
        """Get the root resource."""
        if not self._root:
            self._root = root.Root(root=self)
        return self._root

    @property
    def sessions(self) -> sessions.CampusSessions:
        """Get the sessions resource."""
        if not self._sessions:
            self._sessions = sessions.CampusSessions(root=self)
        return self._sessions

    @property
    def users(self) -> users.Users:
        """Get the users resource."""
        if not self._users:
            self._users = users.Users(root=self)
        return self._users

    @property
    def grants(self) -> grants.Grants:
        """Get the access-grant store resource."""
        if not self._grants:
            self._grants = grants.Grants(root=self)
        return self._grants

    @property
    def vaults(self) -> vaults.Vaults:
        """Get the vaults resource."""
        if not self._vaults:
            self._vaults = vaults.Vaults(root=self)
        return self._vaults

    def exchange_code_for_token(
            self,
            code: str,
            redirect_uri: str
    ) -> campus.model.OAuthToken:
        """Exchange authorization code for access token.

        Makes POST request to /auth/v1/token which atomically:
        - Validates the authorization code
        - Gets or creates credentials for the user
        - Issues a new token or reuses existing valid token
        - Stores the token in credentials
        - Returns the token

        Note: Credential storage is handled automatically by the token endpoint.

        Args:
            code: The authorization code from OAuth callback
            redirect_uri: The redirect URI used in the auth session

        Returns:
            OAuthToken containing access token and metadata

        Raises:
            AuthenticationError: If code is invalid or token exchange fails
        """
        json_body = {
            "grant_type": "authorization_code",
            "code": code,
            "redirect_uri": redirect_uri,
            "client_id": env.CLIENT_ID,
            "client_secret": env.CLIENT_SECRET,
        }
        token_path = self.url_prefix + "/token"
        return campus.model.OAuthToken.from_resource(
            self._post_json(token_path, json=json_body)
        )

    def get_token(self) -> campus.model.OAuthToken:
        """Convenience method to get access token for a user.

        Re-acquires the login session user's campus bearer via
        POST /logins/<session_id>/token (campus#963/#964, invariant
        A10): one Basic-authenticated endpoint call in the
        session-bound lane — never the operator-gated credentials
        routes (#854). An expired grant token is rotated server-side,
        so the returned token is always live; the response carries no
        refresh token.

        Returns:
            OAuthToken for the user

        Raises:
            AuthenticationError: If no login session is present
            APIError: invalid_grant if the login session or the
                user's campus grant is gone — re-login required

        Example:
            # In a protected view that needs the user's token
            token = campus.auth.get_token()
            headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token.id}"}
            response = requests.get("https://api.example.com/data", headers=headers)
        """
        return self.logins.token()

    def token(
            self,
            grant_type: Literal[
                "client_credentials",
                "refresh_token"
            ],
            *,
            refresh_token: str | None = None,
            client_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> campus.model.OAuthToken:
        """Get OAuth token from the token endpoint.

        Targets the RFC 6749 token endpoint (/auth/v1/oauth/token,
        campus/auth/routes/oauth.py), which serves the device_code,
        refresh_token, and client_credentials grants — NOT the
        authorization-code session endpoint at /auth/v1/token
        (campus/auth/provider.py), whose contract requires code and
        redirect_uri and rejects every other grant type (#60).

        The path passed to the client is relative (like every other
        resource method): CampusRequest._build_url() prepends the
        client's base_url itself, so an absolute URL here would be
        double-prefixed into `https://host/https://host/...` and 404
        against real deployments.

        Args:
            grant_type: "client_credentials" or "refresh_token".
            refresh_token: The refresh token to present (refresh_token
                grant).
            client_id: The OAuth client the grant is made as. The token
                endpoint requires client_id for every grant (campus
                auth/routes/oauth.py token()), including refresh_token;
                defaults to CLIENT_ID from the environment (server
                mode). Public clients without CLIENT_ID configured must
                pass it explicitly (issue #87).
        """
        json_body: dict[str, str] = {
            "grant_type": grant_type,
        }
        match grant_type:
            case "client_credentials":
                json_body["client_id"] = env.CLIENT_ID
                json_body["client_secret"] = env.CLIENT_SECRET
            case "refresh_token":
                if not refresh_token:
                    raise errors.AuthenticationError(
                        error_description="Refresh token required for "
                                          "refresh_token grant type."
                    )
                resolved_client_id = client_id or env.get("CLIENT_ID")
                if not resolved_client_id:
                    raise errors.AuthenticationError(
                        error_description="client_id is required for the "
                                          "refresh_token grant; pass it "
                                          "explicitly or set CLIENT_ID."
                    )
                json_body["client_id"] = resolved_client_id
                json_body["refresh_token"] = refresh_token

        token_path = self.url_prefix + "/oauth/token"
        return campus.model.OAuthToken.from_resource(
            self._post_json(token_path, json=json_body)
        )

    def refresh(
            self,
            stored: campus.model.OAuthToken,
            *,
            client_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> campus.model.OAuthToken:
        """Refresh an OAuth token pair (RFC 6749 section 6).

        Takes a stored token and returns the rotated pair issued by the
        server: a new access token with a new refresh token. The
        presented refresh token is single-use — refresh-token grants
        rotate server-side (campus/auth/routes/oauth.py
        _handle_refresh_token_grant) — so the returned token must be
        persisted before the stale one is presented again.

        This is the public-client entry point (issue #87): it needs no
        client secret, only the client_id the stored token was issued
        to. Error responses (invalid_grant, invalid_client, ...) raise
        APIError subclasses carrying the OAuth error code in details,
        readable via APIError.oauth_error.

        Args:
            stored: The stored OAuthToken whose refresh token is
                presented to the server.
            client_id: The OAuth client the token was issued to;
                defaults to CLIENT_ID from the environment (server
                mode).

        Returns:
            The refreshed OAuthToken (new access + refresh tokens).
        """
        if not stored.refresh_token:
            raise errors.AuthenticationError(
                error_description="Stored token has no refresh token; "
                                  "re-authentication is required."
            )
        return self.token(
            grant_type="refresh_token",
            refresh_token=stored.refresh_token,
            client_id=client_id,
        )

class OAuth(ResourceRoot):
    """OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Flow resource.

    Provides methods for device authorization flow used by CLI
    and other applications with limited input capabilities.

    Reference: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8628
    """

    # All OAuth endpoints live under /auth/v1/oauth (campus/auth/routes/
    # oauth.py); the auth app enables strict_slashes, so the slash-less
    # relative paths built here must match the route rules exactly.
    url_prefix = "/auth/v1/oauth"

    def __init__(self, root: ResourceRoot):
        super().__init__(json_client=root.client)
        self._root = root

    def request_device_code(
            self,
            client_id: str,
    ) -> dict:
        """Request a device code for the device authorization flow.

        Args:
            client_id: The OAuth client ID (e.g., "campus-cli")

        Returns:
            Dict containing:
            - device_code: The device code for polling
            - user_code: The code the user must enter
            - verification_uri: The URI where the user enters the code
            - verification_uri_complete: The URI with user_code pre-filled
            - expires_in: Seconds until the device code expires
            - interval: Minimum seconds between polling attempts

        Raises:
            AuthenticationError: If client_id is invalid
        """
        json_body = {
            "client_id": client_id,
        }
        return self._post_json(self.make_path("device_authorize"), json=json_body)

    def poll_for_token(
            self,
            client_id: str,
            device_code: str,
    ) -> dict:
        """Poll the token endpoint for an access token.

        Args:
            client_id: The OAuth client ID
            device_code: The device code received from request_device_code()

        Returns:
            Dict containing:
            - access_token: The access token
            - token_type: Token type (usually "Bearer")
            - expires_in: Seconds until token expires
            - refresh_token: The refresh token
            - scope: Granted scopes

        Raises:
            AuthenticationError: With specific error codes:
            - authorization_pending: User hasn't completed auth yet
            - slow_down: Client is polling too fast
            - expired_token: Device code has expired
            - access_denied: User denied the authorization
        """
        json_body = {
            "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code",
            "client_id": client_id,
            "device_code": device_code,
        }
        resp = self.client.post(self.make_path("token"), json=json_body)

        # Handle OAuth error responses
        if resp.status_code == 400:
            oauth_error, message = _parse_oauth_error(resp.json())

            # Map RFC 8628 errors to AuthenticationError; the OAuth error
            # code travels in details so callers can read it back via the
            # APIError.oauth_error property.
            descriptions = {
                "authorization_pending": "Authorization pending",
                "slow_down": "Slow down",
                "expired_token": "Device code has expired",
                "access_denied": "Access denied by user",
            }
            raise errors.AuthenticationError(
                status_code=400,
                error_description=(
                    descriptions.get(oauth_error or "")
                    or message
                    or "Unknown error"
                ),
                details={"oauth_error": oauth_error},
            )

        resp.raise_for_status()
        return resp.json()

    def wait_for_token(
            self,
            client_id: str,
            device_code: str,
            *,
            interval: int | None = None,
            max_attempts: int = 60,
            on_pending: Callable[[], None] | None = None,
            sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep,
    ) -> dict:
        """Poll the token endpoint until the device is authorized.

        Implements the polling loop RFC 8628 §3.5 clients must run on
        top of poll_for_token(): authorization_pending keeps polling,
        slow_down raises the interval by SLOW_DOWN_ADJUSTMENT seconds
        with the raised interval persisting for the remainder of the
        flow, network failures are retried on non-final attempts, and
        every other error (expired_token, access_denied, unknown) is
        fatal. See the parity table in this module's docstring.

        Args:
            client_id: The OAuth client ID (e.g., "campus-cli")
            device_code: The device code from request_device_code()
            interval: Minimum seconds between poll attempts, from the
                request_device_code() response. Defaults to
                DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL when absent or zero.
            max_attempts: Maximum number of poll attempts; callers
                typically derive this from the device code's expires_in.
            on_pending: Invoked after each authorization_pending response,
                for progress reporting (e.g. printing a dot per poll).
            sleep: The sleep function; injectable for tests.

        Returns:
            The token response dict (access_token, refresh_token, ...),
            as returned by poll_for_token().

        Raises:
            AuthenticationError: On fatal OAuth errors or when
                max_attempts is exhausted without authorization.
            errors.ServerError: When the final attempt fails at the
                network/5xx level.
        """
        poll_interval = (
            max(1, int(interval)) if interval else DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL
        )
        last_attempt = max_attempts - 1

        for attempt in range(max_attempts):
            try:
                return self.poll_for_token(
                    client_id=client_id, device_code=device_code
                )
            except errors.AuthenticationError as err:
                if err.oauth_error == "authorization_pending":
                    if on_pending is not None:
                        on_pending()
                    sleep(poll_interval)
                elif err.oauth_error == "slow_down":
                    # RFC 8628 §3.5: the raised interval persists for
                    # the remainder of the flow, not just the next
                    # attempt.
                    poll_interval += SLOW_DOWN_ADJUSTMENT
                    sleep(poll_interval)
                else:
                    raise
            except errors.ServerError:
                # Network failure: retry on non-final attempts only
                if attempt == last_attempt:
                    raise
                sleep(poll_interval)

        raise errors.AuthenticationError(
            error_description=(
                "Device authorization timed out after "
                f"{max_attempts} poll attempts; restart the flow."
            )
        )

    def authorize_device(
            self,
            user_code: str,
            user_id: str,
    ) -> dict:
        """Authorize a device code with a user ID.

        This is called by the verification page when a user submits
        their user code.

        Args:
            user_code: The user code from the CLI
            user_id: The user ID of the authorizing user

        Returns:
            Dict with success status

        Raises:
            NotFoundError: If user_code is invalid or expired
            ConflictError: If user_code is already authorized/denied
        """
        json_body = {
            "user_code": user_code,
            "user_id": user_id,
        }
        return self._post_json(
            self.make_path("device/authorize"), json=json_body
        )

    def revoke(
            self,
            token: str,
            client_id: str,
            token_type_hint: "str | None" = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Revoke an access or refresh token (RFC 7009).

        Args:
            token: The access or refresh token to revoke
            client_id: The OAuth client the token was issued to
            token_type_hint: Optional "access_token" or "refresh_token"

        Per RFC 7009 section 2.2 the server returns 200 regardless of
        whether the token was found or already revoked, so callers
        cannot use this endpoint to confirm a token's validity.
        """
        self._post_json(self.make_path("revoke"), json=payload(
            token=token,
            client_id=client_id,
            token_type_hint=token_type_hint,
        ))
        return None

class LoginSessions(ResourceCollection):
    """Campus Auth Logins resource."""
    path = "logins"

    def __getitem__(
            self,
            session_id: str | None = None
    ) -> "LoginSessions.Login":
        """Get a login session resource by ID.

        Without an explicit ID, the id resolves from the installed
        session-id provider. There is no framework fallback: hosts
        without a provider must pass the id explicitly.
        """
        session_id = session_id or sessionstore.resolve_session_id(
            sessionstore.LANE_LOGIN
        )
        if not session_id:
            raise errors.AuthenticationError(
                error_description=(
                    "No login session ID available: pass session_id or "
                    "install a session-id provider "
                    "(campus_python.auth.v1.set_session_id_provider)."
                )
            )
        return LoginSessions.Login(session_id, parent=self)

    def from_session(
            self,
            session_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> campus.model.LoginSession:
        """Get a login session using a client-side session ID.

        Resolution order: explicit session_id > the installed
        session-id provider. There is no framework fallback.
        """
        return self[session_id].get()

    def has_session(self) -> bool:
        """True when the installed session-id provider supplies a login
        id for this lane."""
        return bool(sessionstore.resolve_session_id(sessionstore.LANE_LOGIN))

    def token(self, session_id: str | None = None) -> campus.model.OAuthToken:
        """Re-acquire the current login session's campus bearer (#117).

        One endpoint call (campus#964, invariant A10):
        POST /logins/<session_id>/token, authenticated by the client's
        Basic credentials plus the session id — user bearers are denied
        outright, so the caller must not present one (revoke_session()
        first mid-rotation). An expired grant token is rotated
        server-side; the response omits the refresh token.

        The session id resolves explicitly > installed provider.

        Raises:
            AuthenticationError: If no login session is present.
            APIError: invalid_grant when the session or the user's
                campus grant is gone — the cue to require re-login.
        """
        return self[session_id].token()

    def new(
            self,
            *,
            user_id: str,
            device_id: str | None = None,
            agent_string: str,
    ) -> campus.model.LoginSession:
        """Create a new login session.

        Mirrors the payload expected by the logins routes. Storing the
        returned session's id client-side is the host's business
        (flask_campus context owns its flask.session storage).
        """
        client_id = env.CLIENT_ID
        return campus.model.LoginSession.from_resource(self._post_json(
            self.make_path(),
            json=payload(
                client_id=str(client_id),
                user_id=str(user_id),
                agent_string=agent_string,
                device_id=device_id,
            )
        ))

    class Login(Resource):
        """A single login session resource."""

        @property
        def session_id(self) -> str:
            """The login session id embedded in this resource's path."""
            return self.path.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]

        def revoke(self) -> None:
            """Revoke this login session (log the user out)."""
            self._delete_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))

        def get(self) -> campus.model.LoginSession:
            """Get this login session.

            Returns:
                The LoginSession.
            """
            body = self._get_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))
            return campus.model.LoginSession.from_resource(body)

        def update(self, *, expiry_seconds: int) -> campus.model.LoginSession:
            """Extend or shorten this login session.

            Args:
                expiry_seconds: New session lifetime in seconds.

            Returns:
                The updated LoginSession.
            """
            body = self._patch_json(
                self.make_path(end_slash=True),
                json={"expiry_seconds": expiry_seconds}
            )
            return campus.model.LoginSession.from_resource(body)

        def token(self) -> campus.model.OAuthToken:
            """Re-acquire the session user's campus bearer (#117).

            POST /logins/<session_id>/token — the session-bound
            re-acquisition lane (campus#964, invariant A10): the login
            session plays the authorization code's role, authenticated
            with the client's Basic credentials. Issuance mirrors the
            code exchange: an unexpired grant token is reused, an
            expired one is minted fresh (rotated server-side), and a
            missing grant is an invalid_grant, never minted from
            nothing (C5). The response omits the refresh token —
            campus refresh material never leaves the auth service in
            this lane.

            The call presents Basic client credentials, never the
            ambient bearer: the route denies user principals outright
            (#963/A10), and with_user_session() nested inside another
            with_user_session() (e.g. an auth-broker release reached
            from a route that already holds the user session) would
            otherwise present the outer session's user token and be
            refused with 403. Any prior Authorization header is
            restored afterwards, so an enclosing session keeps its
            authorization until it re-runs use_token() with the fresh
            bearer.
            """
            # Canonical path has no trailing slash (route rule is
            # /<session_id>/token, unlike the CRUD subresources).
            prior_authorization = self.client.authorization
            self.client.reset_authorization()
            try:
                body = self._post_json(self.make_path("token"))
            finally:
                if prior_authorization is not None and prior_authorization.startswith(
                        "Bearer "):
                    self.client.set_bearer_authorization(
                        prior_authorization[len("Bearer "):]
                    )
            return campus.model.OAuthToken.from_resource(body)

docs.title: token() -> campus.model.OAuthToken
docs.text:
Re-acquire the session user's campus bearer (#117).

POST /logins//token — the session-bound re-acquisition lane (campus#964, invariant A10): the login session plays the authorization code's role, authenticated with the client's Basic credentials. Issuance mirrors the code exchange: an unexpired grant token is reused, an expired one is minted fresh (rotated server-side), and a missing grant is an invalid_grant, never minted from nothing (C5). The response omits the refresh token — campus refresh material never leaves the auth service in this lane.

The call presents Basic client credentials, never the ambient bearer: the route denies user principals outright (#963/A10), and with_user_session() nested inside another with_user_session() (e.g. an auth-broker release reached from a route that already holds the user session) would otherwise present the outer session's user token and be refused with 403. Any prior Authorization header is restored afterwards, so an enclosing session keeps its authorization until it re-runs use_token() with the fresh bearer.

def token(self) -> campus.model.OAuthToken:
    """Re-acquire the session user's campus bearer (#117).

    POST /logins/<session_id>/token — the session-bound
    re-acquisition lane (campus#964, invariant A10): the login
    session plays the authorization code's role, authenticated
    with the client's Basic credentials. Issuance mirrors the
    code exchange: an unexpired grant token is reused, an
    expired one is minted fresh (rotated server-side), and a
    missing grant is an invalid_grant, never minted from
    nothing (C5). The response omits the refresh token —
    campus refresh material never leaves the auth service in
    this lane.

    The call presents Basic client credentials, never the
    ambient bearer: the route denies user principals outright
    (#963/A10), and with_user_session() nested inside another
    with_user_session() (e.g. an auth-broker release reached
    from a route that already holds the user session) would
    otherwise present the outer session's user token and be
    refused with 403. Any prior Authorization header is
    restored afterwards, so an enclosing session keeps its
    authorization until it re-runs use_token() with the fresh
    bearer.
    """
    # Canonical path has no trailing slash (route rule is
    # /<session_id>/token, unlike the CRUD subresources).
    prior_authorization = self.client.authorization
    self.client.reset_authorization()
    try:
        body = self._post_json(self.make_path("token"))
    finally:
        if prior_authorization is not None and prior_authorization.startswith(
                "Bearer "):
            self.client.set_bearer_authorization(
                prior_authorization[len("Bearer "):]
            )
    return campus.model.OAuthToken.from_resource(body)

class CampusSessions(ResourceCollection):
    """Campus Auth Sessions resource."""
    path = f"sessions/{PROVIDER}"

    def __getitem__(self, session_id: str) -> "CampusSessions.Session":
        return CampusSessions.Session(session_id, parent=self)

    def from_code(self, code: str) -> campus.model.AuthSession:
        """Get a session using authorization code."""
        return campus.model.AuthSession.from_resource(self._post_json(
            self.make_path("authorization_code", end_slash=False),
            json={"code": code}
        ))

    def from_session(self, session_id: str | None = None) -> campus.model.AuthSession:
        """Get a session by its client-side session id.

        Resolution order: explicit session_id > the installed
        session-id provider. There is no framework fallback: hosts
        without a provider must pass the id explicitly.
        """
        if session_id is None:
            session_id = sessionstore.resolve_session_id(
                sessionstore.LANE_SESSION
            )
        if not session_id:
            raise errors.AuthenticationError(
                error_description=(
                    "No session id available: pass session_id or "
                    "install a session-id provider "
                    "(campus_python.auth.v1.set_session_id_provider)."
                )
            )
        return CampusSessions.Session(session_id, parent=self).get()

    def has_session(self) -> bool:
        """True when the installed session-id provider supplies a
        session id for this lane."""
        return bool(sessionstore.resolve_session_id(sessionstore.LANE_SESSION))

    def new(
            self,
            *,
            # expiry_seconds: int,
            user_id: str | None = None,
            redirect_uri: str,
            scopes: "list[str]",
            target: str | None = None,
    ) -> campus.model.AuthSession:
        """Create a new auth session (start the OAuth authorize flow).

        Args:
            user_id: Optional user to pre-authorize.
            redirect_uri: OAuth redirect URI.
            scopes: Scopes to request.
            target: Where to redirect after authorize.

        Returns:
            The created AuthSession.
        """
        client_id = env.CLIENT_ID
        json_data: JsonDict = {
            # "expiry_seconds": expiry_seconds,
            "client_id": client_id,
            "redirect_uri": redirect_uri,
            "scopes": scopes,
        }
        if target is not None:
            json_data["target"] = target
        if user_id is not None:
            json_data["user_id"] = str(user_id)
        # The returned session id doubles as the OAuth state parameter;
        # storing it client-side is the host's business (flask_campus
        # context owns its flask.session storage).
        return campus.model.AuthSession.from_resource(
            self._post_json(self.make_path(), json=json_data)
        )

    def list(
            self,
            *,
            provider: str | None = PROVIDER,
            client_id: str | None = None,
            user_id: str | None = None,
            limit: int | None = None,
            offset: int | None = None,
    ) -> "list[campus.model.AuthSession]":
        """List live sessions (admin view, campus#1055).

        GET /sessions/ with optional provider/client_id/user_id
        filters and limit/offset pagination. Requires the operator
        principal or a designated admin user (sessions:read); client
        principals are denied. Records carry metadata only — no
        authorization_code, no user embeds — and finalized sessions
        are absent (finalize deletes the record).
        """
        query: JsonDict = {}
        if provider is not None:
            query["provider"] = provider
        if client_id is not None:
            query["client_id"] = client_id
        if user_id is not None:
            query["user_id"] = str(user_id)
        if limit is not None:
            query["limit"] = limit
        if offset is not None:
            query["offset"] = offset
        # The list route is provider-agnostic (/sessions/), unlike the
        # campus-provider path this collection wraps.
        collection_path = f"/{self.root.make_path('sessions').strip('/')}/"
        body = self._get_json(collection_path, query=query)
        return [
            campus.model.AuthSession.from_resource(item)
            for item in body.get("sessions", [])
        ]

    def sweep(self, at_time: datetime | str | None = None) -> int:
        """Finalize expired auth sessions.

        Args:
            at_time: Cutoff time (defaults to now, UTC).

        Returns:
            Number of sessions swept.
        """
        json_data: JsonDict = {}
        match at_time:
            case datetime():
                json_data["at_time"] = (
                    schema.DateTime.from_datetime(at_time)
                )
            case str():
                json_data["at_time"] = schema.DateTime(at_time)
            case None:
                json_data["at_time"] = schema.DateTime.utcnow()
        body = self._post_json(self.make_path("sweep", end_slash=False), json=json_data)
        return int(body["swept_count"])

    class Session(Resource):
        """A single provider session (/sessions/campus/{session_id})."""

        @property
        def session_id(self) -> str:
            """The auth session id embedded in this resource's path."""
            return self.path.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]

        def finalize(self) -> "tuple[str, campus.model.User | None]":
            """Finalize this session (post-authorization).

            Returns:
                (target_url, user_or_None): where to redirect the
                browser, plus the session user when the calling client
                owns the session; None from pre-#879 services.
            """
            # DELETE /sessions/{provider}/{session_id} ->
            # {"target": <url>, "user": {...}|null}
            body = self._delete_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))
            # The auth service embeds the session user for the owning
            # client (#879); None from pre-#879 services.
            user = campus.model.User.from_resource(body["user"]) \
                if body.get("user") else None
            return body["target"], user

        def get(self) -> campus.model.AuthSession:
            """Get this auth session.

            Returns:
                The AuthSession.
            """
            body = self._get_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))
            return campus.model.AuthSession.from_resource(body)

        def update(self, **updates) -> None:
            """Update this auth session.

            Only user_id and authorization_code are expected by the
            API; keyword arguments map to session fields.
            """
            # Only user_id and authorization_code are expected by the API
            self._patch_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True), json=updates)
            return None

class Credentials(ResourceCollection):
    """Campus Auth Credentials resource.

    Usage:
    - `creds = Credentials(root=...)`
    - `creds["github"].get(token_id)` -> get by token id
    - `creds["github"][user_id].get(client_id)` -> get credentials for user
    """
    path = "credentials"

    def __getitem__(self, provider: str) -> "Credentials.Provider":
        """Get provider-level collection."""
        return Credentials.Provider(provider, parent=self)

    class Provider(Resource):
        """Provider-level credentials resource.

        Instance `path` is set to include the provider name so that
        requests are made to /{base}/{credentials}/{provider}.
        """

        def __getitem__(self, user_id: str) -> "Credentials.Provider.User":
            """Get a user-specific credential resource."""
            return Credentials.Provider.User(user_id, parent=self)

        def get(
                self,
                token_id: str,
                include_token: bool = False,
        ) -> campus.model.UserCredentials:
            """Get one credential record.

            Reads are redacted by default (campus#1055): the joined
            token carries metadata only. include_token=True opts into
            the raw token — an operator-principal power on the
            service, honored on per-record reads only.
            """
            query: JsonDict = {"token_id": token_id}
            if include_token:
                query["include"] = "token"
            return campus.model.UserCredentials.from_resource(

class Vaults(ResourceCollection):
    """Campus Auth Vaults resource."""
    path = "vaults"

    def __getitem__(self, label: str) -> "Vaults.Vault":
        return Vaults.Vault(label, parent=self)

    def labels(self) -> "list[str]":
        """List vault labels (admin view, campus#1055).

        GET /vaults/ — the operator, the super-admin root, or
        designated users holding any vault grant row plus the
        vaults:read scope; client principals hold per-label access
        only and cannot enumerate.
        """
        return self._get_json(self.make_path()).get("labels", [])

    class Vault(Resource):
        """A single vault (label) exposing mapping-like access."""

        def keys(self) -> "list[str]":
            """List the keys stored in this vault."""
            body = self._get_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True))
            return body["keys"]

        def __delitem__(self, key: str) -> None:
            resp = self.client.delete(self.make_path(key, end_slash=True))
            if resp.status_code == 404:
                raise KeyError(key)
            resp.raise_for_status()
            return None

        def __getitem__(self, key: str) -> str:
            resp = self.client.get(self.make_path(key, end_slash=True))
            # translate 404 into KeyError for route compatibility
            if resp.status_code == 404:
                raise KeyError(key)
            resp.raise_for_status()
            body = resp.json()
            # expected shape: {"key": value}
            return body["key"]

        def __setitem__(self, key: str, value: Any) -> None:
            self._post_json(self.make_path(key, end_slash=True), json={"value": value})
            return None

class Grants(ResourceCollection):
    """Campus Auth access-grant store."""
    path = "grants"

    def list(
            self,
            *,
            grantee_type: "str | None" = None,
            grantee_id: "str | None" = None,
            resource_type: "str | None" = None,
            resource_id: "str | None" = None,
    ) -> JsonDict:
        """List access-grant rows.

        Authorization: unfiltered lists require the operator; user
        principals may list only the single vocabulary they
        administer.

        Args:
            grantee_type: Filter by "user" or "client"
            grantee_id: Filter by grantee identity (user email / client id)
            resource_type: Filter by vocabulary ("users", "clients",
                "vault", ...)
            resource_id: Filter by instance (vault label)

        Returns:
            {"grants": [...]}
        """
        query: JsonDict = {}
        if grantee_type is not None:
            query["grantee_type"] = grantee_type
        if grantee_id is not None:
            query["grantee_id"] = grantee_id
        if resource_type is not None:
            query["resource_type"] = resource_type
        if resource_id is not None:
            query["resource_id"] = resource_id
        return self._get_json(self.make_path(), query=query or None)

    def check(
            self,
            *,
            grantee_type: str,
            grantee_id: str,
            resource_type: str,
            resource_id: str = "",
            bits: "int | None" = None,
            level: "str | None" = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Check whether a grantee's row covers a permission.

        Authorization: operator, or a same-vocabulary admin.

        Args:
            grantee_type: "user" or "client"
            grantee_id: Grantee identity
            resource_type: Vocabulary ("users", "clients", "vault", ...)
            resource_id: Instance (vault label; default none)
            bits: Vault bitflag mask to test
            level: Management level to test

        Returns:
            True when the held row covers the requested permission
        """
        query: JsonDict = {
            "grantee_type": grantee_type,
            "grantee_id": grantee_id,
            "resource_type": resource_type,
        }
        if resource_id:
            query["resource_id"] = resource_id
        if bits is not None:
            query["bits"] = bits
        if level is not None:
            query["level"] = level
        body = self._get_json(self.make_path("check", end_slash=False), query=query)
        return bool(body.get("granted"))

    def grant(
            self,
            *,
            grantee_type: str,
            grantee_id: str,
            resource_type: str,
            resource_id: str = "",
            bits: "int | None" = None,
            level: "str | None" = None,
    ) -> JsonDict:
        """Grant access (create a row, or raise an existing one).

        Authorization: operator, or a same-vocabulary admin. Vault
        bits OR into the existing mask; management levels never
        downgrade — revoke first to lower a level.

        Anti-escalation (#883): no principal may administer its own
        grants, and vocabulary-level clients:admin rows are rejected
        (operator-equivalent).

        Args:
            grantee_type: "user" or "client"
            grantee_id: Grantee identity
            resource_type: Vocabulary ("users", "clients", "vault", ...)
            resource_id: Instance (required for vault labels)
            bits: Vault bitflag mask (vaults only)
            level: Management level (read/mod/write/admin)

        Returns:
            The grant row (post-application state)
        """
        # resource_id or None: "" means "no instance" here, and
        # payload only drops None.
        return self._post_json(self.make_path(), json=payload(
            grantee_type=grantee_type,
            grantee_id=grantee_id,
            resource_type=resource_type,
            resource_id=resource_id or None,
            bits=bits,
            level=level,
        ))["grant"]

    def revoke(
            self,
            *,
            grantee_type: str,
            grantee_id: str,
            resource_type: str,
            resource_id: str = "",
            bits: "int | None" = None,
            level: "str | None" = None,
    ) -> "JsonDict | None":
        """Revoke access (clear vault bits, delete covered levels).

        Authorization: operator, or a same-vocabulary admin. Vault
        rows delete at zero bits; a revoked level's row is deleted
        when the held level covers it.

        Args:
            grantee_type: "user" or "client"
            grantee_id: Grantee identity
            resource_type: Vocabulary
            resource_id: Instance (vault label)
            bits: Vault bitflag mask to clear
            level: Management level to revoke

        Returns:
            The remaining grant row, or None when the row was deleted
        """
        return self._post_json(
            self.make_path("revoke", end_slash=False),
            json=payload(
                grantee_type=grantee_type,
                grantee_id=grantee_id,
                resource_type=resource_type,
                resource_id=resource_id or None,
                bits=bits,
                level=level,
            ),
        )["grant"]

    def delete(self, grant_id: str) -> None:
        """Delete a grant row outright by its id.

        Authorization: operator, or a same-vocabulary admin for the
        row's vocabulary.

        Args:
            grant_id: The grant row's id (from list())
        """
        self._delete_json(self.make_path(grant_id, end_slash=False))

class Connections(ResourceCollection):
    """Campus Auth Connections resource."""
    path = "connections"

    def __getitem__(self, provider: str) -> "Connections.Connection":
        """Get a specific provider's connection resource."""
        return Connections.Connection(provider, parent=self)

    def list(
            self,
            *,
            user_id: "str | None" = None,
    ) -> "list[JsonDict]":
        """List the target user's upstream connections.

        Each entry carries {provider, integration, scopes, connected_at,
        expires_at} — never token values. Auth shape mirrors the server:
        a bearer token acts for its own user (user_id ignored), while
        basic (client-credentials) auth must name a user via user_id.

        Args:
            user_id: Delegated target user (required for basic auth)

        Returns:
            List of connection metadata dicts
        """
        query = {"user_id": user_id} if user_id else None
        return self._get_json(self.make_path(), query=query)["connections"]

    class Connection(Resource):
        """Single provider connection resource."""

        def __getitem__(
                self,
                integration: str,
        ) -> "Connections.Connection.Integration":
            """Get an integration-namespaced connection resource."""
            return Connections.Connection.Integration(
                integration, parent=self
            )

        def delete(self, *, user_id: "str | None" = None) -> None:
            """Disconnect every credential for this base provider.

            404 (NotFoundError) means there was nothing to disconnect;
            callers treating disconnect as idempotent can catch it.

            Args:
                user_id: Delegated target user (required for basic auth)
            """
            query = {"user_id": user_id} if user_id else None
            self._delete_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True), query=query)
            return None

        class Integration(Resource):
            """Integration-namespaced connection resource."""

            def delete(self, *, user_id: "str | None" = None) -> None:
                """Disconnect this provider integration (e.g. google/classroom).

                Args:
                    user_id: Delegated target user (required for basic auth)
                """
                query = {"user_id": user_id} if user_id else None
                self._delete_json(self.make_path(end_slash=True), query=query)
                return None

class Broker(ResourceRoot):
    """Campus Auth token broker resource."""
    url_prefix = "/auth/v1/broker"

    def __init__(self, root: ResourceRoot):
        super().__init__(json_client=root.client)
        self._root = root

    def token(
            self,
            provider: str,
            integration: "str | None" = None,
            *,
            min_scopes: "list[str] | None" = None,
    ) -> JsonDict:
        """Release the bearer's upstream access token for a provider.

        Args:
            provider: Base provider (e.g. "google")
            integration: Integration slug for the namespaced route
                (e.g. "classroom" → /broker/google/classroom/)
            min_scopes: Scopes the caller requires; denied unless the
                user's upstream grant covers them and the client's
                upstream_scopes allowlist permits them

        Returns:
            {provider, user_id, access_token, token_type, expires_in,
            scope} — the refresh token never leaves Campus

        Raises:
            errors.NotFoundError: No connection for this provider
                (404); namespaced providers pointed at the identity
                route are redirected to the integration route the
                same way
            errors.AuthenticationError: Bearer session expired (401)
            errors.APIError: 403 with details.missing_scopes, or 400
                AUTH_INVALID_SCOPE / configuration problems
        """
        if integration:
            path = self.make_path(f"{provider}/{integration}/")
        else:
            path = self.make_path(f"{provider}/")
        return self._post_json(path, json=payload(min_scopes=min_scopes))

def token(
        self,
        provider: str,
        integration: "str | None" = None,
        *,
        min_scopes: "list[str] | None" = None,
) -> JsonDict:
    """Release the bearer's upstream access token for a provider.

    Args:
        provider: Base provider (e.g. "google")
        integration: Integration slug for the namespaced route
            (e.g. "classroom" → /broker/google/classroom/)
        min_scopes: Scopes the caller requires; denied unless the
            user's upstream grant covers them and the client's
            upstream_scopes allowlist permits them

    Returns:
        {provider, user_id, access_token, token_type, expires_in,
        scope} — the refresh token never leaves Campus

    Raises:
        errors.NotFoundError: No connection for this provider
            (404); namespaced providers pointed at the identity
            route are redirected to the integration route the
            same way
        errors.AuthenticationError: Bearer session expired (401)
        errors.APIError: 403 with details.missing_scopes, or 400
            AUTH_INVALID_SCOPE / configuration problems
    """
    if integration:
        path = self.make_path(f"{provider}/{integration}/")
    else:
        path = self.make_path(f"{provider}/")
    return self._post_json(path, json=payload(min_scopes=min_scopes))

class Root(ResourceCollection):
    """Campus Auth root resource."""
    path = "root"

    def authenticate(
            self,
            *,
            token: str | None = None,
            client_id: schema.CampusID | None = None,
            client_secret: str | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Authenticate the given token or client credentials.

        Returns: {
            "client": { ... }
        } or {
            "client": { ... },
            "user": { ... }
        }
        """
        if token:
            body = self._post_json(self.make_path(), json={"token": token})
        elif client_id and client_secret:
            body = self._post_json(
                self.make_path(),
                json={"client_id": client_id, "client_secret": client_secret}

        else:

        if "user" in body:
            body["user"] = campus.model.User.from_resource(body["user"])

campus.python.auth.v1.sessionstore

Client-side session-id resolution seam for the auth session/login lanes.

The SDK never touches a web-framework session store: hosts that keep their session ids in their own request state — e.g. flask_campus, which stores them under sessions.SESSION_STORAGE_KEY / logins.LOGIN_STORAGE_KEY — install a provider that resolves the current id per lane:

from campus_python.auth import v1
v1.set_session_id_provider(my_resolver)

The provider takes a lane name — "session" for auth sessions or "login" for login sessions — and returns the current session id or None. Every read resolves explicit argument first, then the provider; with neither, the resource methods raise AuthenticationError naming the seam to install.

campus_python.Campus is the unified entry point. It resolves one JsonClient per service from the environment (see Getting started › Configuration) and exposes the four service roots plus the token/session managers.

Modes: "server" (default — requires CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET) and "device" (public clients, no credentials). Service base URLs are resolved per service (auth, api, audit) via the campus.common.services registry, in this order: 1. CAMPUS_AUTH_URL / CAMPUS_API_URL / CAMPUS_AUDIT_URL. 2. Bare aliases: AUTH_URL / API_URL / AUDIT_URL. 3. CAMPUS_BASE_URL, then BASE_URL — one origin fronting every service (gateway / single-server deployments).

The environment is the source of truth: Campus ships no baked-in deployment topology, so an unconfigured service raises ValueError.
